title: Inteligência artificial aplicada ao marketing: uma revisão de literatura sobre princípios, composto mercadológico e aplicações ao longo do ciclo de vida do produto
abstract: A inteligência artificial vem transformando o marketing de maneiras que, até pouco tempo atrás, seriam difíceis de imaginar. Neste artigo, busca-se revisitar os fundamentos do campo e examinar como as tecnologias de IA se inserem em cada dimensão do composto mercadológico, da criação do produto ao atendimento pós-venda. A pesquisa segue uma abordagem qualitativa, sustentada por revisão bibliográfica de publicações indexadas nas bases Scopus, Web of Science e Google Scholar, com recorte temporal entre 2015 e 2024. Os achados mostram que a IA amplia de forma relevante a capacidade de personalização da experiência do consumidor, a precisão na precificação, a segmentação de mercado, a automação de campanhas e a gestão do relacionamento com o cliente. A conclusão aponta que o uso estratégico da IA no marketing pode gerar vantagem competitiva duradoura, contanto que seja orientado por princípios éticos sólidos e pelo compromisso genuíno com a criação de valor para o consumidor.

title: Comparative analysis of deep learning techniques in bone tumor detection and classification
abstract: Bone tumors are a significant medical concern to identify since they are complicated, and there are diagnostic methods that are invasive, slow, and inaccurate.Consequently, deep-learning (DL) methods of bone tumor detection and classification are receiving interest. They are alleged to be more precise, quicker and easier to integrate into clinical practice. This research analyses current advancements in deep learning systems for the detection and classification of bone tumours. This study contrasts current methods with novel deep learning methodologies, evaluates the efficacy of cutting-edge systems, and proposes future research areas for bone tumour diagnosis.

title: Natural language processing for sentiment analysis in social media cybersecurity threat detection
abstract: The presence of social media platforms in the marketing world is nothing but a double-edged sword, on one hand, they are powerful but on the other hand, they are the carriers of the cybersecurity threats because of the text-centric aspect they got. The present research deals with the use of sentiment analysis—a subfield of NLP—for the probing of the digital chats. The categorization of user sentiment by means of these models can lead to the detection of potential threat language through the application of a high degree of contextual precision. One of the most important features of this method is that it is capable of processing data in real-time which enables organizations to move from a reactive to a proactive security model. Furthermore, this work delves into the challenges of scaling this detection across multiple languages and defending against deliberate adversarial attacks designed to evade sentiment classification.

title: Banglablend Based Evaluation of Bengali Formal and Colloquial Text Classification
abstract: Bangla, one of the most widely spoken languages globally, exhibits a significant diglossic nature characterized by two primary stylistic forms: Sadhu Bhasha (formal/classical) and Cholito Bhasha (colloquial). With the proliferation of digital communication, the blending of these styles often leads to grammatical inconsistency and challenges in computational processing. This study presents a comprehensive comparative analysis for the stylistic classification of Bengali text using the BanglaBlend dataset, comprising 7,350 balanced instances. A diverse range of models is evaluated across three categories: traditional Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), and Transformer-based Natural Language Processing (NLP) architectures. Our experimental results indicate a clear performance hierarchy, where Transformer models significantly outperform traditional approaches. Specifically, XLM-RoBERTa achieved the highest performance with an accuracy of 94 % and an F1score of 0.94, closely followed by Bangla-BERT at 93.4%. Deep Learning models like CNN and BiLSTM also showed robust results, reaching 92% accuracy, whereas traditional ML models plateaued at 81 %. These findings underscore the necessity of contextualized embeddings and self-attention mechanisms in capturing the nuanced morphological and syntactic patterns of the Bangla language, providing a robust foundation for downstream tasks such as stylistic normalization, content moderation, and sentiment analysis.

title: Adaptive FinTech Intelligence with Fraud Detection and Customer Segmentation Using Supervised and Unsupervised Learning for Industry 5.0
abstract: Fraud is one of the most serious risks in FinTech. Every day, millions of digital transactions are processed, and many fraudulent activities go undetected. Traditional rule-based systems struggle as fraud patterns evolve and class imbalance makes detection more difficult. This research uses both unsupervised and supervised learning under the Industry 5.0 framework. Unsupervised models such as K-Means, DBSCAN, and MeanShift are used for customer segmentation. They help find hidden groups, spending patterns, and anomalies. Supervised models such as XGBoost, Random Forest, and LightGBM are used for fraud detection. Results show XGBoost gives 99.9% accuracy and 8.9% precision, but a low recall of 44%. Random Forest gives 93. 5% recall but only 8.7% precision. LightGBM gives a balanced result with an AUC of 0.83. Using anomalies from clustering with supervised models improves adaptability to new fraud types. The combined method supports better customer insight and fraud detection. This creates a stronger and more reliable FinTech system. It also matches the goals of Industry 5.0 by making systems adaptive, intelligent, and human-centered. The approach highlights how integrating different machine learning strategies can enhance resilience. It also provides a scalable framework that financial institutions can apply to safeguard digital transactions in real time.

title: Translive: Conceptual Design of an AI-Driven Real-Time Multilingual Speech Translation Framework
abstract: Growing global needs are driving increased demand for instantaneous cross-language communication across education, healthcare, enterprise collaboration, and public interaction. Notwithstanding significant progress in artificial intelligence-driven translation, many existing solutions depend on closed cloud-based platforms that can introduce processing delays, limit customizability, and raise privacy concerns. This paper presents a conceptual framework for TransLive, a component-based frame-work for instantaneous spoken-language conversion designed to deliver scalable and privacy-aware multilingual communication on mobile devices. The proposed framework integrates Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Neural Machine Translation (NMT), and Text-to-Speech (TTS) modules in a streaming microservice pipeline designed to produce parallel translations across several target languages. A central concept is performing ASR once and translating the resulting text into several languages in parallel, enabling listeners to receive continuous translated audio in their preferred language. Although conceptual, this work outlines the theoretical foundation, architecture, mobile integration strategy, evaluation plan, and real-world applications for TransLive.

title: Does RL Expand the Capability Boundary of LLM Agents? A PASS@(k,T) Analysis
abstract: Does reinforcement learning genuinely expand what LLM agents can do, or merely make them more reliable? For static reasoning, recent work answers the second: base and RL pass@k curves converge at large k. We ask whether this holds for agentic tool use, where T rounds of interaction enable compositional strategies that re-sampling cannot recover. We introduce PASS@(k,T), a two-dimensional metric that jointly varies sampling budget k and interaction depth T, separating capability expansion from efficiency improvement. Our main finding is that, contrary to the static-reasoning result, tool-use RL genuinely enlarges the capability boundary: the RL agent's pass-curve pulls above the base model's and the gap widens at large k rather than converging. The expansion is specific to compositional, sequential information gathering; on simpler tasks RL behaves as prior work predicts. Under matched training data, supervised fine-tuning regresses the boundary on the same compositional tasks, isolating self-directed exploration as the causal factor. Mechanism analysis shows RL reweights the base strategy distribution toward the subset whose downstream reasoning more often yields a correct answer, with the improvement concentrated on how the agent integrates retrieved information. These results reconcile optimistic and pessimistic readings of RL for LLMs: both are correct, on different task types.

title: Quantifying Cross-Query Contradictions in Multi-Query LLM Reasoning
abstract: Large language models frequently produce mutually inconsistent answers when reasoning over multiple related queries. We study case-file logical consistency: maintaining a globally satisfiable belief state across interdependent queries. We introduce a benchmark of 390 multi-query reasoning instances with entailment/contradiction/unknown labels and propose set-level metrics including Case Satisfiability Rate, Contradiction Density and Revision Cost. Our solver-augmented approach extracts commitments, verifies global satisfiability and performs counterexample-guided repair. Across four reasoning domains, our method substantially reduces cross-query contradictions (SetCons: 0.56 to 0.94) while preserving per-query accuracy, demonstrating that global coherence is critical for robust multi-query reasoning.

title: The Explanatory Constraint Knife: Why Representational Accounts Fail in Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Contemporary artificial intelligence systems are frequently described as possessing representations, internal world models, or understanding-like states. These descriptions persist despite repeated failures in reliability, grounding, and generalization. This paper argues that such failures are not incidental but structural. We introduce the Explanatory Constraint Knife (ECK): a criterion that distinguishes genuine explanation from representational description. Under ECK, an explanation is valid only insofar as it constrains what cannot occur. Representational accounts, we argue, systematically fail this criterion. They describe internal correlations but do not enforce exclusion. As a result, they misclassify perceptual fluency as understanding and optimization success as explanatory adequacy. This paper establishes ECK as a necessary epistemic filter for AI explanation and prepares the ground for subsequent analyses of hallucination and long-horizon failure.

title: CervScan : Predictive Model to Detect Cervical Diseases
abstract: Cervical cancer remains the leading cause of mortality to women all over the world, and, therefore, we require early, precise, and comprehendible diagnostic systems. The Cervical Cancer Cell Image Dataset is used in this study to show a full automated deep learning framework for cervical cancer cell analysis. The framework consists of classification, detection, explainability and web-based application. Transfer learning-based convolutional neural networks such as ResNet50, DenseNet201, InceptionV3, and Xception were used as initial points in classifying the images. In order to enhance the capability of making the distinction, a hybrid feature-level fusion mechanism was proposed. This approach involves DenseNet201 and InceptionV3 mixture, principal component analysis (PCA), and lastly a fully connected neural network (FNN). We further considered more hybrid configurations with DenseNet201-ResNet50 feature fusion + PCA and deep FNN, and a residual multilayer perceptron (Residual MLP) to improve the gradient flow and the robustness. DenseNet201 achieved the highest results in classifying with accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score (F1-score=98.0). YOLOv5, YOLOv8, YOLOv9, and YOLOv11 object recognition models were tested for finding abnormal cells and classifying them at the same time. YOLOv9 performed the best, with precision 0.575, recall 0.697, and mAP 0.646. To perform visual interpretation, explainable AI based on Grad-CAM was employed. Lastly, the system was put into practice with the help of a Flask-based web application to do real-time clinical inference.

title: Citechat: A Rag Based Intelligent Chatbot
abstract: CiteChat is a document-based intelligent chatbot, which uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to provide correct and context-sensitive answers of documents stored by users, including resumes, research papers and articles. It will take into account the fact that the proposed system will offer more factual consistency as compared to conventional large language model (LLM) systems because it will base every one of its responses on the uploaded document. A stringent grounding procedure is put in place to avoid the production of unsupported answer generation by introducing similarity threshold validation which minimizes hallucination. First, the PDF documents are read with the help of transformer-based sentence embeddings, and the embeddings are stored in the local memory, preserving the data privacy but allowing the data to be easily retrieved. When the user enters a query, the semantic similarity search mechanism finds the most relevant document segments and the most relevant document segments are made available to a Groq-powered LLaMA model to generate the response. The system also increases the level of transparency by including page-level snippets of citations and generated answers along with calculation of a retrieval-based confidence score to show the reliability of answers. Experimental analysis shows better factual basis and fewer hallucination in contrast to the standalone approaches based on the LLM. Lastly, the lightweight Streamlit interface helps to upload documents and interactively query, making it easy to analyze documents.

title: MGMIN-FSA: A Multi-Granularity Multimodal Interaction Network for Sentiment Analysis of Financial Review Videos
abstract: Automated sentiment analysis of extensive financial review videos provides investors with a precise understanding of market sentiment. However, compared to videos in other domains, financial review videos contain extensive financial jargon and exhibit more nuanced sentiment changes in facial expressions and vocal tones. Most traditional models focus solely on either coarse-grained or fine-grained multimodal sentiment expression. This limitation renders them ineffective in handling videos with subtle sentiment changes, restricting their applicability to analysing sentiment in financial review videos. This paper introduces the Multi-Granularity Multimodal Interaction Network (MGMIN-FSA) for analysing sentiment in financial review videos. First, the Fine-grained Multimodal Interaction Network (FMN) is presented, incorporating Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) and attention mechanisms to extract crucial phrase-level features across modalities, producing fine-grained sentiment expressions. Additionally, KAN-Attention within FMN improves the model's generalization capability. Second, the Coarse-grained Feature Decoupling Network (CFDN) is introduced, establishing anchors at both modal and sentiment feature levels to improve differentiation between positive and negative samples. Finally, MGMIN-FSA integrates fine- and coarse-grained representations for sentiment analysis using downstream classifiers. MGMIN-FSA obtains the best performance on the FMSA-SC and CH-SIMS datasets among all compared methods. Furthermore, experimental results demonstrate that KAN-Attention can maintain high performance despite insufficient data.

evidence.title: MGMIN-FSA: A Multi-Granularity Multimodal Interaction Network for Sentiment Analysis of Financial Review Videos
evidence.abstract: Automated sentiment analysis of extensive financial review videos provides investors with a precise understanding of market sentiment. However, compared to videos in other domains, financial review videos contain extensive financial jargon and exhibit more nuanced sentiment changes in facial expressions and vocal tones. Most traditional models focus solely on either coarse-grained or fine-grained multimodal sentiment expression. This limitation renders them ineffective in handling videos with subtle sentiment changes, restricting their applicability to analysing sentiment in financial review videos. This paper introduces the Multi-Granularity Multimodal Interaction Network (MGMIN-FSA) for analysing sentiment in financial review videos. First, the Fine-grained Multimodal Interaction Network (FMN) is presented, incorporating Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) and attention mechanisms to extract crucial phrase-level features across modalities, producing fine-grained sentiment expressions. Additionally, KAN-Attention within FMN improves the model's generalization capability. Second, the Coarse-grained Feature Decoupling Network (CFDN) is introduced, establishing anchors at both modal and sentiment feature levels to improve differentiation between positive and negative samples. Finally, MGMIN-FSA integrates fine- and coarse-grained representations for sentiment analysis using downstream classifiers. MGMIN-FSA obtains the best performance on the FMSA-SC and CH-SIMS datasets among all compared methods. Furthermore, experimental results demonstrate that KAN-Attention can maintain high performance despite insufficient data.

title: Bridging the Domain Gap in Waste Detection: A Self-Training Approach for Cross-Environment Generalization
abstract: Domain shift is one of the primary hindrances in deploying deep-learning-based waste detection systems in real-world settings because of a significant performance decline when models are applied to environments that are visually distinct from their training data. This study proposes an unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) framework using a self-training approach to alleviate this gap. The proposed model generates high-confidence pseudo-labels for an unlabeled target domain and iteratively adapts them without human annotation. We achieved a mAP@0.5 of 0.314, which is a substantial improvement over the baseline direct transfer performance of 0.101 and recovered 42.3% of the performance gap to a fully supervised upper bound (0.605). Therefore, this study demonstrates a practical and effective approach for scalable and robust waste detection systems that are capable of operating across diverse urban environments.

title: A Hybrid BanglaBERT–Ensemble Framework for Cyberbullying Detection in Bengali and Chattogram Dialects
abstract: Cyberbullying in Bengali social media remains a serious problem. Dialectal variation increases this challenge. Most existing studies focus on standard Bengali text. Limited attention is given to regional dialects. Current methods often rely on a single feature type. This causes performance loss on complex language patterns. In this study, cyberbullying detection is investigated using Bengali and Chattogram text. A hybrid architecture is proposed. Contextual features are extracted using BanglaBERT. Statistical and semantic features are added using TF-IDF and Word2Vec. Feature fusion is applied to enrich representation. Classification is performed using the Extra Trees ensemble model. A publicly available Bengali cyberbullying dataset is used. Manual transliteration is applied to generate Chattogram data. Class imbalance is handled using oversampling. Experimental results show strong performance. The BanglaBERT with Extra Trees model achieves up to 92.95% accuracy. The proposed approach outperforms existing methods. Robust detection across dialects is ensured. This framework supports safer Bengali online communication.

title: An Adaptive Computer-Assisted Language Learning System Using Recurrent Neural Networks and Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: An adaptive computer-assisted language learning (CALL) system is an advanced technology used to create a customized language-learning experience while increasing student participation. This study describes the development of a unique adaptive CALL framework using Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) and Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) for automatic feedback and individualized English language acquisition. The proposed approach uses sequential textual and auditory input to evaluate a learner's grammatical structure, pronunciation, and sentences; based on this data, an adaptive reinforcement learning process continuously modifies task/evaluation complexity, feedback techniques and paths to knowledge through the relationship of state, action and reward. By performing experimental tests, an overall training accuracy of 92 % was achieved and an 88 % validation success was recorded, demonstrating steady growth and effective transferability. The adaptations made from the adaptive learning process improved resultant language proficiency by$\mathbf{2 2} \boldsymbol{\%}$to$\mathbf{2 6 \%}$, lowered the number of recurring learner errors by 37 %, and increased the level of learner engagement by approximately 35 %. This study shows how the combination of deep and reinforcement learning enhances and adapts today's computer-assisted language learning model.

title: El Agente Forjador: Task-Driven Agent Generation for Quantum Simulation
abstract: AI for science promises to accelerate the discovery process. The advent of large language models (LLMs) and agentic workflows enables the expediting of a growing range of scientific tasks. However, most of the current generation of agentic systems depend on static, hand-curated toolsets that hinder adaptation to new domains and evolving libraries. We present El Agente Forjador, a multi-agent framework in which universal coding agents autonomously forge, validate, and reuse computational tools through a four-stage workflow of tool analysis, tool generation, task execution, and iterative solution evaluation. Evaluated across 24 tasks spanning quantum chemistry and quantum dynamics on five coding agent setups, we compare three operating modes: zero-shot generation of tools per task, reuse of a curriculum-built toolset, and direct problem-solving with the coding agents as the baseline. We find that our tool generation and reuse framework consistently improves accuracy over the baseline. We also show that reusing a toolset built by a stronger coding agent can reduce API cost and substantially raises the solution quality for weaker coding agents. Case studies further demonstrate that tools forged for different domains can be combined to solve hybrid tasks. Taken together, these results show that LLM-based agents can use their scientific knowledge and coding capabilities to autonomously build reusable scientific tools, pointing toward a paradigm in which agent capabilities are defined by the tasks they are designed to solve rather than by explicitly engineered implementations.

title: A Technology-Enhanced Learning Perspective on Educational Robotics in Vocational Teacher Education
abstract: This chapter explores the transformative role of educational robotics as a Technology-Enhanced Learning (TEL) tool in vocational teacher education within Industry 4.0. Robotics equips educators with digital literacy, creativity, and adaptability, preparing learners for technology-driven workplaces. Drawing on constructivist and constructionist theories, the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework, and 21st-century skills, the chapter shows how robotics fosters problem-solving, collaboration, and competency-based training. Case studies from Africa, alongside perspectives from Asia, Europe, and North America, highlight successes and challenges. Barriers at institutional, teacher, and student levels are analysed, with solutions emphasising policy alignment, collaboration, and professional development. Future directions include AI-driven robotics, virtual labs, and global partnerships. The chapter concludes that educational robotics is a strategic necessity for creating equitable, sustainable, and future-ready vocational teacher education worldwide.

title: XGBoost-Deep Residual (FedXGB-ResNet) collaborative porosity prediction in a federated learning framework
abstract: Privacy protection and multimodal fusion represent significant challenges in the context of cross-institutional geological data collaboration. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a collaborative XGBoost-Deep Residual model (FedXGB-ResNet) within a federated learning framework to achieve high-accuracy porosity prediction. Through a heterogeneous federated integration architecture, the framework combines XGBoost’s efficient modeling of structured well-logging parameters (with a feature importance gain of 41.2%) with ResNet’s deep extraction of spatiotemporal features from seismic images (87% overlap in activation maps between training and validation sets). The model achieved R2 scores of 0.87 and 0.83 on North Sea and Bakken oilfield datasets, respectively, representing improvements of 12.7% and 9.3% over the traditional FedAvg-XGBoost baseline. The innovative dual privacy protection mechanisms—gradient obfuscation and Paillier encryption—suppressed the membership inference attack success rate to 13.7% and reduced gradient similarity to 0.19 at a noise scale of 1.5 (privacy budget = 0.75), while increasing communication time by only 23%. A dynamic feature distillation mechanism adaptively fuses multimodal features through gated attention units, narrowing the F1-score gap between high-porosity and lowporosity identification to 5%. Experiments demonstrated that the framework reduces the risk of privacy leakage by 84.7% while retaining 93.4% of the performance of a centralized model, offering a balanced solution for collaborative cross-domain geological data analysis in terms of accuracy, privacy, and efficiency.

title: Machine learning for smarter network traffic classification: A comprehensive survey
abstract: In today&s;s communication systems, preserving Quality of Service (QoS), guaranteeing network security, and improving bandwidth efficiency all depend on efficient network traffic classification. Because of the increase in encrypted traffic and dynamic applications, traditional classification techniques like port-based and payload-based classification are no longer dependable. Alternatively, Machine Learning (ML) methods provide greater flexibility and accuracy by automatically recognising patterns in the statistical properties of network flows. Using the popular KDD dataset for intrusion and traffic classification, this study compares a number of machine learning methods, such as Adaboost, KNN, SVM, C4.5 Decision Trees, Logistic Regression, and Random Forest. Pre-processed, feature-extracted, labelled data were used to train and evaluate each method. According to experimental results, the Random Forest model outperformed all other approaches in terms of accuracy and robustness. The results emphasize how crucial it is to choose the right algorithm that will be used by smart traffic classification systems. They also reveal the possible use of ensemble learning models in real network applications, which can be very valuable.

title: Transformer-Based Sentence Reconstruction from Jumbled Words: A Comparative Evaluation Against Sequence Models
abstract: The task of reconstructing grammatically and semantically correct sentences from jumbled words, also known as typoglycemia, continues to remain difficult in NLP because of the presence of lexical ambiguity with disruption to the normal word order. In this paper, we present a comparative study of sentence-level jumbled word correction using statistical, recurrent, and transformer-based models. In preparation for this, we create an internally permuted version of a set of clean English sentences, preserving the boundary characters (spaces/punctuation), to create a supervised dataset. We compare six approaches: signature-based statistical baseline, LSTM, BiLSTM, T5, BART, and a weighted ensemble model. Exact Match, BLEU, ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, and ROUGE-L are considered as the performance metrics. Experimental results demonstrate that the recurrent models failed to generalize well, reaching near-zero Exact Match scores. Transformer-based models significantly outperform them. Among all methods, the best performance is achieved by BART with 0.318 Exact Match, 0.836 BLEU, and 0.912 ROUGE-L, while achieving high reconstruction accuracy and fluency. This finding underlines the effectiveness of pre-trained denoising transformers in reconstructing jumbled sentences, while establishing a strong baseline for future studies in robust text correction.

title: BlockFlow: A Scalable Blockchain Integrated Federated Learning Framework for Decentralized Aggregation and Incentive Driven Collaboration
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables privacy-preserving collaborative machine learning, yet centralized aggregation suffers from model integrity risks, participation collapse, and scalability limitations. We present BlockFlow, a blockchain-integrated FL framework featuring: (1) decentralized aggregation via smart contracts with Merkle commitments and zk-SNARKs, (2) reputation-weighted Shapley-value incentives, and (3) hierarchical sharding achieving 15-20× throughput improvement. BlockFlow achieves 99.3% attack detection accuracy, 78% participation improvement, and 1,200 updates/sec throughput while maintaining convergence guarantees under blockchain delays.

title: Exploring LIME and Its Variant to Explain Breast Cancer Image Classification in Neural Networks
abstract: Computer-aided diagnosis systems based on deep learning have demonstrated great potential for the diagnosis of breast cancer from mammographic images. However, their application in real-world settings is still limited. The biggest drawback in using these systems in real-world settings is the lack of transparency and interpretability of the decision-making process. This paper proposes a comparative framework for Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) that investigates the impact of different architectures on the clinical utility of explanations. Five different architectures—Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Fully Connected Neural Networks (MLP), VGG16 (Visual Geometry Group - 16 layers) using transfer learning, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU)—are trained as binary classifiers on a carefully selected small and imbalanced subset of the CBIS-DDSM mammography dataset of 1,000 images. Rather than emphasizing overall accuracy, the study emphasizes the malignant recall rate, which is of utmost importance in clinical diagnosis. Of all the architectures, VGG16 performs best with a validation accuracy of 0.85 and a malignant recall rate of 0.85. For the analysis of interpretability, Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) is used for image-based spatial models. The results show that the quality of explanations is highly dependent on whether the architecture maintains spatial information. CNN-based models provide spatial explanations that are clinically interpretable, while sequential models with high accuracy provide explanations that are not spatially consistent and hence are not clinically interpretable. This paper proposes the idea of Comparative Architectural Interpretability and shows that explainability methods are not able to bridge architectural gaps in medical image analysis tasks. The results provide valuable insights for the development of transparent, trustworthy, and reliable AI systems for the diagnosis of breast cancer.

title: Late Breaking Results: Hardware-Aware Compilation Reshapes Trainability in Variational Quantum Circuits
abstract: Variational quantum circuits (VQCs) are typically evaluated at the logical design level when analyzing trainability. However, execution on real quantum devices requires hardware-aware compilation (transpilation) to satisfy qubit connectivity and native gate-set constraints. In this paper, we examine how transpilation can alter the gradient statistics. Using parameter-shift differentiation and gradient variance estimation, we compare logical and transpiled circuits across three representative ansatz families: EfficientSU2 (dense entanglement), TTN (tree tensor network), and RealAmplitudes (linear entanglement). We observe architecture-dependent trainability shifts where densely entangling circuits exhibit pronounced gradient reshaping in shallow regimes, structured tensor-network circuits remain comparatively robust, and linear architectures show mixed behavior. Deep circuits across all families display minimal sensitivity to hardware-aware compilation. These findings demonstrate that transpilation acts as an implicit structural transformation of the optimization landscape, motivating compilation-aware analysis and co-design for VQCs.

title: Forecasting the future with LESSR
abstract: Forecasting the future with LESSR Professor David Gerbing of Portland State University developed lessR to make professional-quality data visualization and forecasting accessible to everyone – at no cost and with minimal effort. Anyone with a computer can freely download R along with its user-friendly development environment, RStudio. To help beginners get started quickly, Professor Gerbing also developed a companion website for students that provides step-by-step setup instructions and numerous practical examples.

title: ORKG weekly snapshots
abstract: This dataset contains two archives: orkg.tar.gz: 34 weekly snapshots of the Open Research Knowledge Graph (ORKG), exported in N-Triples (.nt) RDF format. The snapshots were collected automatically on a weekly basis and cover a consecutive period of 34 weeks. Each file (1.nt through 34.nt) corresponds to a full dump of the ORKG knowledge graph at the time of export, enabling longitudinal analysis of the graph's growth, evolution, and change over time. alldata.TB.nq.gz: a versioned dataset containing the triples from all 34 snapshots with an IRI in the fourth position (quad) containing all versions in which the triple is valid (BEAR versioning approach) The timestamps from which the snapshots originate are: 20250515, 20250522, 20250527, 20250608, 20250612, 20250619, 20250626, 20250703, 20250710, 20250717, 20250724, 20250731, 20250807, 20250814, 20250821, 20250828, 20250904, 20250911, 20250918, 20250925, 20251002, 20251009, 20251016, 20251023, 20251030, 20251106, 20251113, 20251120, 20251127, 20251204, 20251211, 20251218, 20251225, 20260129 The ORKG (https://orkg.org) is a scholarly infrastructure developed and maintained by TIB – Leibniz Information Centre for Science and Technology, Hannover, Germany. It aims to describe research papers in a structured, machine-readable way to support FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) scholarly communication. License: CC0 1.0 Universal (Public Domain Dedication) The ORKG data is published under CC0 1.0, with the exception of data sourced from Papers With Code, which is licensed under CC BY-SA. Users working with subsets of this data that originate from Papers With Code should comply with the CC BY-SA license terms accordingly.

title: Computing Descriptive Statistics and Anomaly Detection on Station Data
abstract: This experiment processes raw station measurement files (NumPy arrays) to compute descriptive statistics and detect anomalies for each station. It reads all .npy files from the data directory, calculates summary metrics and anomaly counts, and saves the results as a JSON file and a CSV summary. A separate step then generates a formatted text report from the computed statistics. Outputs include output/statistics.json, output/summary.csv, and output/report.txt. ## How to Reproduce Requirements: Docker must be installed and running. **Windows:** runExperiment.bat **Linux / macOS:** bash runExperiment.sh

title: Understanding Consumer Responses to Robotic Cafés: A Person–Environment Interaction Perspective
abstract: Technological advancements in automation and artificial intelligence are transforming the coffee shop experience, with a major industry shift driven by robot baristas whose capabilities differ from those of existing self-service technologies and other hospitality operations. However, understanding consumers’ adoption and experiences remains unclear. To bridge this gap, two studies were conducted based on South Korea as the empirical setting ( N = 670). Specifically, Study 1 examined how different personality traits influence consumers’ affective responses and word-of-mouth behaviors using Latent Profile Analysis, and Study 2 investigated how the social servicescape affects customer experience and behavioral loyalty in robotic service models with Structural Equation Modeling. Data from consumers who have experienced either of the different robotic coffee shop models reveal significant differences in affective experiences and word-of-mouth behaviors across the two personality profiles. Servicescape dimensions are significant predictors of affective experiences and word-of-mouth behaviors. These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of consumer behavior in automated service environments, offering valuable insights for businesses seeking to optimize customer experience and adoption strategies in the coffee shop industry.

title: Robust and Size-Optimized Error Handling in Rust for Resource-Constrained Embedded Systems
abstract: Reliable error handling is essential in embedded firmware, where failures cannot be isolated by an operating system and improper fault management may compromise functionality and security. This work investigates the influence of Rust's error-handling mechanisms on firmware efficiency, focusing on the trade-off between panic-based termination and explicit Result propagation.

title: The BOOL.I Corpus: The Impact of Context on Child and Adolescent Bengali ASR
abstract: This paper presents a Bangladeshi Bangla speech corpus for children and adolescents and evaluates state-of-theart Bengali Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models on this data. Although significant progress has been made in the construction of Bangladeshi Bangla corpora, dedicated resources for young speakers remain relatively underexplored. Our corpus contains 16,069 segmented utterances from speakers aged 5 to 18 years and is designed to support research on child and adolescent speech in Bangladeshi Bangla. Using a four-stage evaluation framework consisting of preprocessing, unified inference, error computation, and WER distribution analysis, we benchmark four leading pretrained models: bengali-whisper-medium and three wav2vec2-xls-r-300m variants. bengali-whisper-medium achieves the strongest performance with a Micro WER of 0.4092 and a Micro CER of 0.2131, outperforming all wav2vec2 based systems. A fine-grained analysis shows that 16.47% of segments achieve perfect recognition and 22.71% fall within WER$\approx 0.37$). This finding reveals that contextual information helps ASR systems overcome acoustic variability in children's speech, demonstrating the critical role of context-aware modeling for young speakers.

title: BanglaSarcThematic: A Transformer-Based Approach Towards Fine-Grained Thematic Sarcasm Analysis Using a Novel Dataset
abstract: Sarcasm detection in Bengali texts presents unique challenges due to complex linguistic structures and cultural nuances. While existing approaches focus on binary classification (sarcasm or non-sarcasm), this paper introduces BanglaSarcThematic, the first transformer-based framework for finegrained thematic sarcasm analysis in Bengali. We contribute a comprehensive dataset of$\mathbf{1 2, 4 1 0}$manually annotated Bengali social media comments with five labels: non-sarcasm and four thematic sarcasm categories (non-thematic, geopolitical, hate expression, and entertainment sarcasm). Our methodology evaluates two classification strategies using six state-of-the-art transformer models: BERT-based models for bidirectional contextual understanding and contrastive models for discriminative semantic learning. We compare direct five-class classification against hierarchical two-stage classification. Our hierarchical approach demonstrates effectiveness through specialized model selection: Stage 1 achieves 84.21% binary classification(sarcasm or non-sarcasm) accuracy using BanglaBERT, while Stage 2 achieves 88.75% accuracy on thematic classification of sarcastic content using BGE-M3 Embedding. The end-to-end pipeline yields 77.13% overall accuracy compared to 76.15% for direct five-class classification. The superior performance of specialized models at different stages validates the effectiveness of hierarchical classification for capturing thematic nuances in Bengali sarcastic discourse, establishing new benchmarks for lowresource language sarcasm detection.

title: Personality-Driven Consequence Reasoning (PDCR): A Five-Layer Deliberative Architecture for Consequence-Aware Household Robotics
abstract: Carrying out multi-step tasks in unstructured environments has been significantly improved with recent Vision-Language-Action (VLA) architectures-based models for household robots. Existing systems still tend to be primarily reactive, maximizing short-horizon task success but without directly reasoning about downstream safety, social or user-dependent consequences. This limitation, which we call consequence blindness, induces a gap between task competence and real-world acceptability in human-centric environments. We propose the Personality-Driven Consequence Reasoning (PDCR), a deliberative framework where multi-dimensional consequence evaluation is directly integrated into the robot decision loop. We propose to split control in two: a high-speed reactive path and a consequence-aware evolution module at the high level to evaluate candidate trajectories according to physical risk, safety, social acceptability and task-functional dimensions. Additionally, this framework integrates an uncertainty-aware user model to update soft behavioral preferences while maintaining fixed hard safety constraints. We instantiate the proposed architecture as a modular embodied stack and evaluate it on simulated, immersive household tasks and safety-critical planning. The results obtained after using the PDCR algorithm show that the actual state of the system is maintained along with the uncertainty estimation on personality probabilities are minimized as compared to existing reactive systems, which makes it executed in a safe environment.

title: GIST: Multimodal Knowledge Extraction and Spatial Grounding via Intelligent Semantic Topology
abstract: Navigating complex, densely packed environments like retail stores, warehouses, and hospitals poses a significant spatial grounding challenge for humans and embodied AI. In these spaces, dense visual features quickly become stale given the quasi-static nature of items, and long-tail semantic distributions challenge traditional computer vision. While Vision-Language Models (VLMs) help assistive systems navigate semantically-rich spaces, they still struggle with spatial grounding in cluttered environments. We present GIST (Grounded Intelligent Semantic Topology), a multimodal knowledge extraction pipeline that transforms a consumer-grade mobile point cloud into a semantically annotated navigation topology. Our architecture distills the scene into a 2D occupancy map, extracts its topological layout, and overlays a lightweight semantic layer via intelligent keyframe and semantic selection. We demonstrate the versatility of this structured spatial knowledge through critical downstream Human-AI interaction tasks: (1) an intent-driven Semantic Search engine that actively infers categorical alternatives and zones when exact matches fail; (2) a one-shot Semantic Localizer achieving a 1.04 m top-5 mean translation error; (3) a Zone Classification module that segments the walkable floor plan into high-level semantic regions; and (4) a Visually-Grounded Instruction Generator that synthesizes optimal paths into egocentric, landmark-rich natural language routing. In multi-criteria LLM evaluations, GIST outperforms sequence-based instruction generation baselines. Finally, an in-situ formative evaluation (N=5) yields an 80% navigation success rate relying solely on verbal cues, validating the system's capacity for universal design.

title: Explain the Flag: Contextualizing Hate Speech Beyond Censorship
abstract: Hate, derogatory, and offensive speech remains a persistent challenge in online platforms and public discourse. While automated detection systems are widely used, most focus on censorship or removal, raising concerns for transparency and freedom of expression, and limiting opportunities to explain why content is harmful. To address these issues, explanatory approaches have emerged as a promising solution, aiming to make hate speech detection more transparent, accountable, and informative. In this paper, we present a hybrid approach that combines Large Language Models (LLMs) with three newly created and curated vocabularies to detect and explain hate speech in English, French, and Greek. Our system captures both inherently derogatory expressions tied to identity characteristics and direct group-targeted content through two complementary pipelines: one that detects and disambiguates problematic terms using the curated vocabularies, and one that leverages LLMs as context-aware evaluators of group-targeting content. The outputs are fused into grounded explanations that clarify why content is flagged. Human evaluation shows that our hybrid approach is accurate, with high-quality explanations, outperforming LLM-only baselines.

title: Anomaly Detection in Financial Transactions
abstract: Abstract: Financial fraud is an ever-growing threat in the global banking and e-commerce landscape, costing organizations billions of dollars each year. Anomaly detection — the process of identifying patterns in data that deviate significantly from expected behavior — has emerged as a cornerstone of modern fraud prevention systems. This research paper presents a comprehensive review and comparative analysis of machine learning techniques applied to anomaly detection in financial transactions, with a focus on their effectiveness, scalability, and real-world applicability. We examine supervised methods such as Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost; unsupervised approaches including Isolation Forest, Local Outlier Factor (LOF), and Autoencoders; and hybrid ensemble frameworks. Special attention is given to the challenge of highly imbalanced datasets — a persistent issue in fraud detection — and techniques such as SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique) and cost-sensitive learning are evaluated as remedies. Experimental results on the publicly available IEEE-CIS Fraud Detection and PaySim datasets demonstrate that ensemble methods and deep learning autoencoders yield the highest AUC-ROC scores, reaching up to 0.98. The paper further discusses real-world implementation challenges, ethical considerations, regulatory compliance (including GDPR), and future directions such as federated learning and explainable AI (XAI) in fraud detection. Keywords: Anomaly Detection, Financial Fraud, Machine Learning, Isolation Forest, Autoencoder, Imbalanced Data, XGBoost, Deep Learning, SMOTE, Federated Learning

title: Admissible Operator Optimisation: Selection and Efficiency Within Constraint Boundaries
abstract: This paper defines admissible operator optimisation within the Paton System, establishing how execution paths are selected and evaluated under constraint. Building on the Paton Operator Calculus and Operator Stability frameworks, this work formalises how systems choose among multiple admissible paths while preserving viability. It introduces efficiency as a constrained measure, where optimisation is permitted only within admissible regions and must not compromise continuation. The framework introduces no new domain-specific laws and does not modify governing equations. It operates as a pre-theoretical layer determining how admissible paths are ranked, selected, and maintained under constraint. This paper is part of the Paton Operator Layer and is structurally linked with: - The Paton Operator Calculus: Composition, Sequencing, and Admissible Execution Paths - Operator Stability and Failure: Admissibility Breakdown Under Sequential Constraint Together, these define how systems construct, degrade, and select execution paths under constraint. title: Bengali Political Narrative Understanding via Transformer Models for Web Applications
abstract: The rise of Web 3.0 and widespread internet growth in Bangladesh has transformed political engagement and social media platforms have become the central lifeline to the public political discourse. This digital move has intensified political polarization and increased the spreading of misinformation. This environment of ideological conflict underscores the need for robust sentiment analysis tools tailored towards Bengali. While sentiment classification has been widely studied in high-resource settings, Bengali political sentiment for multi-class classification remains underexplored due to limited annotated corpora. Our work presents a supervised multiclass sentiment classification framework specifically for Bengali political text where the limitation of binary sentiment models has been addressed. This will remove the challenges of oversimplification of nuanced expressions that were not considered by binary models. The proposed model utilizes the categorization of political sentiment divided into five classes to help us capture ideological intensity and emotional polarity more effectively. We fine-tuned the XLMRoBERTa transformer model on a curated political corpus and leverages its multilingual capabilities and contextual embeddings to enhance performance in low-resource settings. Experimental results demonstrated strong classification performance across sentiment categories. The model achieved a macroF1-score of$\mathbf{7 6 \%}$, with class-wise$\mathbf{F 1}$-scores of$\mathbf{6 7 \%}$(negative),$\mathbf{8 4 \%}$(Neutral),$\mathbf{7 1 \%}$(Positive),$\mathbf{7 5 \%}$(Very Negative), and 82% (Very Positive). Precision and recall values were consistently high for neutral and extreme sentiment classes. This indicated the model's robustness in capturing polarized expressions. Confusion matrix analysis revealed overlaps between adjacent sentiment class labels and multiclass ROC curves confirmed reliable separability. These findings validated the model's effectiveness for political sentiment monitoring across multiple classes.

title: FedEPL+:Carbon-Aware Client Selection With Valid Differential Privacy in Federated Learning
abstract: The generation of large volumes of data due to smart city surveillance needs distributed learning solutions that are benign in data leaks and carbon cost. However, current privacypreserving FL frameworks often treat privacy and climate goals as opposing objectives. FedEPL+ (Federated Eco-Pprivate Learning +) is proposed with adaptive central differential privacy, emission-aware client scheduling and hierarchical aggregation. A Multi-Armed Bandit (MAB) scheduler matches computation with low-carbon energy windows. It also comes with a strict adaptive gradient clipping. FedEPL+ incorporates a robust Rényi Differential Privacy (RDP) accounting mechanism to address the analytic deficiencies of traditional privacy amplification outcomes in the context of adaptive, emission-sensitive participant selection. It is calibrated considering maximum inclusion probability ($q_{\max }$), which provides a strong safeguard against underestimating privacy loss caused by data-driven scheduling. On CIFAR-10 simulation experiments, the accuracy of FedEPL+ is$86.0 \pm 2.0 \%$for strict privacy budgets ($\epsilon=3.0, \delta=10^{-5}$). The estimated carbon emission of FedEPL+ is$\mathbf{3 7. 5 \%}$smaller than private baselines. Moreover, the client starvation variance is only 0.08.

title: SCATR: Simple Calibrated Test-Time Ranking
abstract: Test-time scaling (TTS) improves large language models (LLMs) by allocating additional compute at inference time. In practice, TTS is often achieved through parallel scaling: generating multiple candidate responses and selecting the best via a Best-of-N (BoN) strategy. Its effectiveness therefore hinges on the scoring function. Learned scorers such as process reward models (PRMs) can be strong, but they are expensive to train and run. Lightweight confidence heuristics based on token log-probabilities are much cheaper, yet we find that they often perform substantially worse. To improve on lightweight confidence heuristics without incurring the full cost of stronger learned scorers, we introduce SCATR, a simple and efficient BoN ranking method that learns a lightweight scorer from a small calibration set using hidden representations from the base model. Across coding and mathematical reasoning benchmarks, SCATR improves over prior confidence-based baselines by up to 9%. Relative to LoRA fine-tuning on the same calibration data, it achieves comparable accuracy with up to 8000x fewer trainable parameters and much lower compute, reducing training and inference latency by up to 150x and 1000x, respectively. SCATR is also competitive with strong PRM baselines, and in several settings improves accuracy by up to 7.8% on math and 4.2% on coding while enabling up to 1000x faster inference. Overall, SCATR offers a strong accuracy-efficiency trade-off for scalable test-time selection.

title: O3LS: Optimizing Lattice Surgery via Automatic Layout Searching and Loose Scheduling
abstract: Toward the large-scale, practical realization of quantum computing, quantum error correction is essential. Among various quantum error-correcting codes, the surface code stands out as a leading candidate, and lattice surgery based on surface codes has emerged as a promising technique for fault-tolerant quantum computation (FTQC). However, implementing quantum algorithms using lattice surgery introduces both resource and time overhead. Existing approaches typically focus on large layout designs, with compiler passes aimed primarily at optimizing time overhead. This often overlooks the trade-off between rotation bottlenecks and movement distance, which leads to inefficient resource utilization and prevents further reduction of the quantum computation failure rate. To address these challenges, we introduce O3LS, a framework for optimizing lattice surgery through automatic layout search and loose scheduling. O3LS achieves an optimal balance by automatically generating squeezed data layouts to reduce space requirements and employing loose scheduling algorithms combined with circuit synthesis techniques to reduce time overhead, thereby effectively minimizing overall logical error rates. Numerical results indicate that O3LS can reduce space overhead by 28.0% over standard layouts and 46.7% over sparse layouts without increasing the number of time steps, leading to suppression of logical error rates by up to 16% relative to larger data layout designs. O3LS can also achieve time overhead reductions of 36.07% and 24.76% in compact and standard data layout designs, respectively. It suppresses logical error rates by up to an order of magnitude compared to prior compilers that focus primarily on maximizing parallelism.

title: Efficient Fuzzy Private Set Intersection from Secret-shared OPRF
abstract: Private set intersection (PSI) enables a sender holding a set $Q$ of size $m$ and a receiver holding a set $W$ of size $n$ to securely compute the intersection $Q \cap W$. Fuzzy PSI (FPSI) is a PSI variant where the receiver learns the items $q \in Q$ for which there exists some $w \in W$ satisfying $\mathsf{dist}(q, w) \le δ$ under a given distance metric. Although several FPSI works are proposed for $L_{p}$ distance metrics with $p \in [1, \infty]$, they either heavily rely on expensive homomorphic encryptions, or incur undesirable complexity, e.g., exponential to the element dimension, both of which lead to poor practical efficiency. In this work, we propose efficient FPSI protocols for $L_{p \in [1, \infty]}$ distance metrics, primarily leveraging significantly cheaper symmetric-key operations. Our protocols achieve linear communication and computation complexity in the set sizes $m,n$, the dimension $d$, and the distance threshold $δ$. Our core building block is an oblivious programmable PRF with secret-shared outputs, which may be of independent interest. Furthermore, we incorporate a prefix technique that reduces the dependence on the distance threshold $δ$ to logarithmic, which is particularly suitable for large $δ$. We implement our FPSI protocols and compare them with state-of-the-art constructions. Experimental results demonstrate that our protocols consistently and significantly outperform existing works across all settings. Specifically, our protocols achieve a speedup of $12{\sim}145\times$ in running time and a reduction of $3{\sim}8\times$ in communication cost compared to Gao et al.~(ASIACRYPT'24) and a speedup of $9{\sim}80\times$ in running time and a reduction of $5{\sim}19\times$ in communication cost compared to Dang et al.~(CCS'25).

title: On-Demand Microwave Single-Photon Source Based on Tantalum Thin Films
abstract: Single-photon sources are crucial for quantum information technologies. Here, we demonstrate a microwave single-photon source based on tantalum thin films, whose favorable material properties enable high-quality and stable photon emission. The antibunching behavior of the emitted radiation is revealed by second-order correlation measurements. Furthermore, traveling-wave parametric amplifiers are used as low-noise pre-amplifiers in the detection chains, substantially improving the signal-to-noise ratio and thereby greatly reducing the acquisition time required for second-order correlation measurements. These results demonstrate the viability of tantalum-based superconducting devices as reliable platforms for microwave quantum photonics.

title: Can AI Invent a Language or Write a Novel?
abstract: Episode summary: Could an AI invent a new language from scratch, write a novel people actually finish, or author an original movie script? We break down these creative frontiers, assessing what's technically possible now versus what's been genuinely achieved. The analysis reveals a consistent gap between generating superficially correct outputs and creating works with deep coherence, intent, and aesthetic life. Show Notes The question of whether artificial intelligence can be genuinely creative—inventing languages, writing novels, or authoring screenplays—cuts to the core of what current systems can and cannot do. This exploration assesses three specific frontiers, separating technical possibility from meaningful achievement. **Inventing a Language** Technically, AI can generate the description of a language: lists of words, grammatical rules, and phonemes. Researchers have conducted experiments where models, trained on linguistic data, produce outputs labeled as new conlangs. However, these creations consistently lack the internal consistency, depth, and generative logic of a real constructed language like Tolkien's Elvish. The AI paints a picture from the outside, assembling features that statistically resemble language without a guiding aesthetic principle or embodied understanding. The critical gap is between description and embodiment. A human conlanger builds from a seed concept, feeling the constraints and possibilities of the system they are creating. An AI, by contrast, samples probable linguistic features from its training data. It cannot use its own invented language to express novel thoughts or handle complex translation tasks with true understanding. While there are AI-assisted conlang tools, the driving creative intelligence—the "why" behind the language's structure—remains human. **Writing a Novel** Generating 200,000 syntactically correct words is technically feasible. The market is already flooded with AI-generated text labeled as novels. Yet, producing a book that is structurally coherent, emotionally engaging, and worth reading cover-to-cover is a vastly different challenge. On its own, AI fails to maintain narrative consistency over long-form works, forgetting character details, introducing plot contradictions, and lacking a sustained authorial voice. The more promising path is collaboration. There are documented cases, particularly in genre fiction like romance, where authors use AI for ideation, drafting scenes, and dialogue polish while maintaining strict human control over plot architecture, character consistency, and emotional pacing. These AI-assisted books can achieve commercial viability, but a *good* book authored solely by AI, meeting a high literary standard, remains unrealized. The gap is one of long-range narrative coherence and emotional truth. **Authoring a Screenplay** The highly structured format of a screenplay might seem ideal for AI generation. Models can now produce scripts with proper formatting, scene headings, and dialogue that mimics professional screenwriting. Landmark experiments like the short film "Sunspring" demonstrated the surreal, incoherent results of earlier systems. While outputs today look more polished, they suffer from derivative plots, shallow character motivations, and an inability to handle subtext. A great screenplay relies on what is unspoken and on audience expectations being carefully set and paid off. AI, which operates by predicting the next token based on explicit training data, is ill-equipped to manage the implicit layers of meaning that define quality storytelling. No AI has produced an original, feature-length screenplay that stands on its own merits without significant human rewriting and editorial direction. **The Common Thread** Across all three domains, a pattern emerges. Current AI excels at generating artifacts that match the *form* of creative works—a grammar textbook, a manuscript, a script. However, it struggles with the *function*: creating something with internal logic, sustained coherence, and, most importantly, intentionality. The systems lack a guiding aesthetic goal or a model of the world they are building. They are sophisticated remix engines, not originators. The frontier of AI creativity, therefore, lies not in autonomous authorship but in its potential as a powerful collaborative tool in the hands of a human director who provides the essential vision, consistency, and "why. Listen online: https://myweirdprompts.com/episode/ai-creative-frontiers-language-novel

title: Evaluating Ontology Property Restrictions: A Benchmark Dataset
abstract: Benchmark Overview Supported Tasks We construct a benchmark dataset based on student-built ontologies to enable the experimental investigation of four knowledge engineering sub-tasks: Detection of modeling issues Classification of modeling issues Explanation of modeling issues Generation of alternative modeling solutions as possible corrections Contents The benchmark contains axioms that include the following OWL property restrictions: Existential restrictions (owl:someValuesFrom) Universal restrictions (owl:allValuesFrom) Cardinality restrictions owl:minQualifiedCardinality owl:maxQualifiedCardinality owl:qualifiedCardinality Creation and Further Details The complete methodology for creating the benchmark is described in the following publication: Tsaneva, S., Herwanto, G. B., Llugiqi, M., and Sabou, M. Knowledge Engineering with Large Language Models: A Capability Assessment in Evaluating Ontology Property Restrictions. Submitted to Semantic Web Journal (Under Review) View Publication Sample Test Dataset Sample.csv To facilitate the piloting of the expert annotation of the benchmark, 14 axioms (15%) were annotated by two experts each in an initial evaluation round. These 14 axioms were excluded from the final benchmark and can be used to pilot experimental investigations. Benchmark Dataset Benchmark-NoEval.csv The complete set of axioms is provided without the expert annotation to prevent potential data leaks into the training data of large language models. The complete dataset including expert annotations can be provided upon request. LLM Dataset Additional datasets produced during the experimental investigations are also available. These include outputs of 4 LLMs: GPT 4o (gpt-4o-2024-08-06) Claude Sonnet 3.7 (claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219) Llama 3.3 (Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo) DeepSeek V3 (version from 2024/12/26) on the 4 knowledge engineering subtasks (detection, classification, explanation and generation). The complete additional datasets including expert annotations can be provided upon request.

title: Accuracy of Deep Learning for Detecting Axillary Lymph Node Metastasis in Breast Cancer: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
abstract: Background: Axillary lymph node metastasis (ALNM) is an important factor in detecting breast cancer (BC). However, the noninvasive diagnosis of ALNM remains challenging. While some deep learning (DL) models have been developed for preoperative ALNM assessment, their performance lacks systematic evaluation. Objective: This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of DL in detecting ALNM, providing evidence to support clinical diagnostic tools. Methods: Embase, Web of Science, PubMed, and Cochrane Library were searched from their inception through January 26, 2026. The Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies was used to assess the risk of bias in the included studies. A bivariate mixed effects model was applied for analysis, and subgroup analyses were conducted based on different imaging modalities. Results: This meta-analysis included 28 independent studies and pooled data from 20,811 patients with BC. Among them, 7123 cases had confirmed ALNM. The overall diagnostic performance of the DL model (bivariate mixed effects) for detecting ALNM in BC was as follows: sensitivity 0.80 (95% CI 0.76-0.84), specificity 0.85 (95% CI 0.80-0.88), diagnostic odds ratio (DOR) 22 (95% CI 16-30), and area under the summary receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) 0.89 (95% CI 0.86-0.92). The positive likelihood ratio (LR+) was 5.2 (95% CI 4.1-6.5), and the negative likelihood ratio (LR-) was 0.24 (95% CI 0.19-0.29). For ultrasound-based DL models targeting ALNM detection, the pooled sensitivity and specificity were 0.79 (95% CI 0.72-0.84) and 0.86 (95% CI 0.79-0.91), respectively. Diagnostic performance metrics showed an LR+ of 5.5 (95% CI 3.8-8.1), an LR- of 0.25 (95% CI 0.19-0.32), a DOR of 22 (95% CI 15-33), and an AUC of 0.89 (95% CI 0.86-0.91). Regarding magnetic resonance imaging-based DL models for detecting ALNM, the pooled sensitivity was 0.78 (95% CI 0.71-0.83) and the pooled specificity was 0.82 (95% CI 0.76-0.87). Corresponding metrics included an LR+ of 4.4 (95% CI 3.3-5.9), an LR- of 0.27 (95% CI 0.21-0.35), a DOR of 16 (95% CI 11-25), and an AUC of 0.87 (95% CI 0.84-0.90). For computed tomography (CT)-based models, the sensitivity was 0.90 (95% CI 0.78-0.96), the specificity was 0.88 (95% CI 0.84-0.92), and the AUC was as high as 0.91 (95% CI 0.89-0.94). Conclusions: Current DL methods for detecting ALNM in BC primarily utilize ultrasound, magnetic resonance imaging, and CT. DL models based on all 3 modalities demonstrated good diagnostic performance. CT had the highest sensitivity and AUC, while its specificity was comparable to that of ultrasound. These findings provide supportive evidence for the development or optimization of clinical diagnostic models.

Regarding magnetic resonance imaging-based DL models for detecting ALNM, the pooled sensitivity was 0.78 (95% CI 0.71-0.83) and the pooled specificity was 0.82 (95% CI 0.76-0.87). Corresponding metrics included an LR+ of 4.4 (95% CI 3.3-5.9), an LR- of 0.27 (95% CI 0.21-0.35), a DOR of 16 (95% CI 11-25), and an AUC of 0.87 (95% CI 0.84-0.90). For computed tomography (CT)-based models, the sensitivity was 0.90 (95% CI 0.78-0.96), the specificity was 0.88 (95% CI 0.84-0.92), and the AUC was as high as 0.91 (95% CI 0.89-0.94). DL models based on all 3 modalities demonstrated good diagnostic performance. CT had the highest sensitivity and AUC, while its specificity was comparable to that of ultrasound. title: A Transformer-Based Perspective to Bangla-English Code-Mixed Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Despite Bangla being the seventh most spoken language worldwide, it remains a low-resource language in Natural Language Processing, particularly concerning Bangla-English (BE) code-mixed text. While Banglish (transliterated Bangla) has been studied, sentiment analysis of text containing native Bangla script alongside English words remains underexplored. This paper addresses this gap by introducing BE-CodeMix-3, a manually annotated sentiment dataset of 8,179 social media comments categorized into three sentiment classes. We provide a comprehensive evaluation across various architectures, including traditional Recurrent Neural Networks (LSTM, BiLSTM, GRU) and transformer-based models (mBERT, XLMRoBERTa, and BanglaBERT). Experimental results demonstrate that language-specific pretraining is critical for capturing the nuances of code-mixed text. The BanglaBERT model significantly outperforms all baselines, achieving a peak accuracy and F1-score of 0.90. Our findings highlight that while multilingual models provide a strong foundation, transformers pretrained specifically on large-scale Bangla corpora offer superior semantic and syntactic encoding for real-world, codemixed applications.

title: A Unified Evaluation of Preprocessing, Feature Representation, and Modeling Strategies for Bangla Social Media Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Sentiment analysis for Bangla social media text remains challenging due to informal spelling, code-mixing, dialectal variation, and heavy use of emojis and noisy punctuation. This study presents a unified experimental evaluation of preprocessing, feature representation, and modeling strategies for Bangla sentiment classification. Study construct a cleaned sentiment corpus of approximately 2350 Bangla social media comments labeled into Negative, Neutral, and Positive, and perform a stratified 80/20 train–test split. Study evaluate traditional machine learning baselines using TF-IDF representations (Logistic Regression, Linear SVM, and Naïve Bayes) and compare them against a fine-tuned transformer-based model using BanglaBERT. To improve efficiency and robustness, implementation pipeline integrates emoji normalization, noise handling, pre-tokenization, dynamic padding, mixed precision training, and class-weighted loss. Experimental results show that the fine-tuned BanglaBERT substantially outperforms all baseline methods, achieving 0.70 accuracy and 0.69 macro-F1, while the best baseline (TF-IDF + Logistic Regression) achieves 0.55 macro-F1. Error analysis via the confusion matrix indicates that Neutral sentiment remains the most challenging class due to ambiguity and overlap with polarized expressions. The findings confirm that transformerbased contextual representations, combined with targeted preprocessing, provide a strong foundation for Bangla sentiment analysis in noisy social media environments.

title: Relevance Structures Are a Necessary Prerequisite for Artificial Metacognition
abstract: AI-enabled systems deployed in dynamic, open-world, safety- and mission-critical environments often lack mechanisms for reliable self-monitoring and self-regulation under shift and perturbation. Artificial Metacognition (AM) addresses this by enabling systems to assess and adapt their own inference and learning processes. We show that relevance structures, which are order-theoretic substrates for comparing generalization and specialization and for quantifying under-coverage versus overreach, are structurally unavoidable for computable self-regulation. In turn, relevance structures provide an operational control theory for metacognitive tasks. We introduce exploratory, parsimonious, and balanced relevance scores and embed them into version-space algebra to regulate hypothesis search and inductive strategy selection. The resulting framework yields competence-aware learning systems that can both correct and explain their behavior by explicitly balancing exploration and parsimony. We illustrate relevance structures and their application with a medical visual question answering study on the SLAKE dataset.

title: An Intelligent Online Banking Framework with Real-Time Transaction Streaming and ML-Based Fraud Detection
abstract: The explosion in the number of online financial transactions has led to a major rise in the threat of fraudulent financial activities necessitating smart and scalable fraud detection mechanisms. This paper presents a graph-based framework for detecting anomalies in financial transactions, which combines the concepts of machine learning and network analysis to detect suspicious financial transactions. Transaction data are represented as a collection of interaction graphs linking users, devices, IP addresses and products, allowing for the representation of complex behavioral relationships that cannot easily be illustrated in tabular format. Node2Vec is used to create embeddings that are low dimensions and are based on the structure of the graph. These embeddings have been analyzed by two unsupervised algorithm techniques-Aisolation Forest and DBSCAN respectively responsible for anomaly scoring and the density-based clustering to identify the outlier nodes. A FastAPI based backend is used to support real-time transaction processing, anomaly validation, JWT-Based and Role based access controls. A real-time monitoring and analysis are allowed via an interactive (react-based) dashboard. Experimental results conducted on synthetic transaction data show the effectiveness of the proposed framework to detect anomalous patterns of transactions, which is a clear evidence of scalability and practicality.

title: vstash: Local-First Hybrid Retrieval with Adaptive Fusion for LLM Agents
abstract: We present **vstash**, a local-first document memory system that combines vector similarity search with full-text keyword matching via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) and adaptive per-query IDF weighting. All data resides in a single SQLite file using sqlite-vec for approximate nearest neighbor search and FTS5 for keyword matching. We make four primary contributions. **(1)** Self-supervised embedding refinement via hybrid retrieval disagreement: across 753 BEIR queries on SciFact, NFCorpus, and FiQA, 74.5% produce top-10 disagreement between vector-heavy (vec=0.95, fts=0.05) and FTS-heavy (vec=0.05, fts=0.95) search (per-dataset rates 63.4% / 73.4% / 86.7%, Section 5.2), providing a free training signal without human labels. Fine-tuning BGE-small (33M params) with MultipleNegativesRankingLoss on 76K disagreement triples improves NDCG@10 on all 5 BEIR datasets (up to +19.5% on NFCorpus vs. BGE-small base RRF, Table 6). On 3 of 5 datasets, under different preprocessing, the tuned 33M-parameter pipeline matches or exceeds published ColBERTv2 results (110M params) and an untrained BGE-base (110M); on FiQA and ArguAna it underperforms ColBERTv2 (Section 5.5). **(2)** Adaptive RRF with per-query IDF weighting improves NDCG@10 on all 5 BEIR datasets versus fixed weights (up to +21.4% on ArguAna), achieving 0.7263 on SciFact with BGE-small. **(3)** A negative result on post-RRF scoring: frequency+decay, history-augmented recall, and cross-encoder reranking all failed to improve NDCG. **(4)** A production-grade substrate with integrity checking, schema versioning, ranking diagnostics, and a distance-based relevance signal validated on 50,425 relevance-judged queries across the 5 BEIR datasets. Search latency remains 20.9 ms median at 50K chunks with stable NDCG. The fine-tuned model is published as `Stffens/bge-small-rrf-v2` on HuggingFace. All code, data, and experiments are open-source.

title: Simulation of quantum annealing on a semiconducting cQED device for Multiple Hypothesis Tracking (MHT) benchmark
abstract: We explore the expected performance of a semiconducting spin cQED quantum processor for Multiple Hypothesis Tracking (MHT) algorithm via a quantum annealing procedure. From two different benchmarking scenarios we evaluate this type of quantum annealer on a quantum emulator in which we incorporated both dynamical coherent errors and incoherent errors. From estimate of the reset, measurement and annealing time of the processor, we find that cQED-spin processors could reach a total run time of around 50 ms. This makes this technology promising for potential real time application such as radar tracking.

title: HyperSpace: A Generalized Framework for Spatial Encoding in Hyperdimensional Representations
abstract: Vector Symbolic Architectures (VSAs) provide a well-defined algebraic framework for compositional representations in hyperdimensional spaces. We introduce HyperSpace, an open-source framework that decomposes VSA systems into modular operators for encoding, binding, bundling, similarity, cleanup, and regression. Using HyperSpace, we analyze and benchmark two representative VSA backends: Holographic Reduced Representations (HRR) and Fourier Holographic Reduced Representations (FHRR). Although FHRR provides lower theoretical complexity for individual operations, HyperSpaces modularity reveals that similarity and cleanup dominate runtime in spatial domains. As a result, HRR and FHRR exhibit comparable end-to-end performance. Differences in memory footprint introduce additional deployment trade-offs where HRR requires approximately half the memory of FHRR vectors. By enabling modular, system-level evaluation, HyperSpace reveals practical trade-offs in VSA pipelines that are not apparent from theoretical or operator-level comparisons alone.

title: Toxic to Positive Comment Rewriting using Supervised Fine-Tuning and Direct Preference Optimization
abstract: The increased use of harmful, offensive, and disre-spectful language online can be attributed to the rapid growth of social media platforms. Although many existing systems focus on detecting and removing harmful content and toxic comments, this approach does not always encourage constructiveText detoxification is a challenging Natural Language Pro- cessing (NLP) task that requires controlled text generation and contextual understanding. In this study, we propose a transformer-based system for rewriting toxic comments that utilizes both Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO).
