title: Energy-Aware Federated Learning for Climate Monitoring
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) plays a vital role in climate monitoring, biodiversity assessment, and disaster prediction; however, traditional centralized AI models demand high computational power and energy, increasing carbon emissions. This chapter introduces an energy-aware Federated Learning (FL) framework that decentralizes model training across distributed sensors to minimize communication overhead, preserve data privacy, and reduce energy consumption. By employing lightweight models, adaptive aggregation, and renewable-powered infrastructure, the framework achieves accurate, low-carbon environmental intelligence. It positions FL as a sustainable “green AI” solution for scalable, privacy-conscious, and climate-resilient monitoring systems.

title: MuDPK: Knowledge Distillation With Multi-Granularity and Dynamic Priors for Graph Classification
abstract: Knowledge distillation technology shows significant potential in transferring the knowledge of graph neural network (GNN) teacher models to multi-layer perceptron (MLP) student models. However, the existing methods are primarily designed for node classification task and are difficult to directly apply to graph classification. Graph classification task requires knowledge transfer via the generation of graph-level soft labels. Such global supervisory signals are inherently sparse, making it difficult for the student model to capture fine-grained structural information. Additionally, the student MLP model lacks the explicit ability to handle graph structures and has a significantly different representation space from the teacher GNN which further complicates the knowledge transfer process. We address these problems by proposing multigranularity distillation with a dynamic prior knowledge framework named MuDPK. The proposed framework integrates multigranularity structural information with the dynamic prior knowledge mechanism to effectively address the challenges of sparse supervision signals and the representation bottleneck in graph classification. We first design an adaptive graph propagation-based node feature enhancement module to enhance the representation capability of the student model in a limited feature space. We then design a triple distillation loss function that includes graph-level, subgraph-level, and node-level components. We alleviate the problem of sparse supervision signals by hierarchically aligning the structural representations of the teacher-student model at different levels. Finally, we use the intermediate layer features of the teacher as both the target representation and input knowledge, dynamically adjusted by our prior knowledge mechanism. Knowledge transfer is achieved through feature alignment while the student model is regulated by adjusting the proportion of injected knowledge in a controlled manner. Extensive experiments on eight benchmark graph datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of MuDPK, which achieves an average accuracy gain of +1.37% over the baselines.

title: A Comparative Study of Classical and Hybrid Quantum Machine Learning Models for Skin Lesion Classification Using Latent Feature Embeddings
abstract: This study investigates the potential of Hybrid Quantum Machine Learning (HQML) to improve the classification of skin lesions, a critical task for early detection of skin cancer. We utilized latent feature representations extracted by a Mobile CLIP model from a skin lesion dataset. These features were classified using three leading classical machine learning (ML) models-Logistic Regression (LR), Gradient Boosting (GB), and Support Vector Machine (SVM)-and compared against two quantum models: the Quantum Kernel Support Vector Machine (QSVM) and a Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC). All models were trained on features reduced to$\mathbf{4}$dimensions via PCA. The results indicate that while classical models achieved high overall accuracy (GB: 0.9452, LR: 0.9424, SVM: 0.9292), they struggled significantly with the minority class (malignant lesions). The SVM achieved the highest recall for the minority class (0.36), outperforming LR (0.32) and GB (0.17). The QSVM achieved 100 % accuracy on the initial synthetic test data, while the VQC achieved an accuracy of 0.8933. These results highlight the potential of quantum feature spaces to enhance separability, establishing a baseline for further exploration of HQML in robust clinical decision support.

title: Federated Learning Enhancing Fraud Detection Across Multiple Financial Institutions
abstract: In this paper, Research discuss how Federated Learning can be used to improve fraud detection across various financial institutions using a new model that is built on Federated Reinforcement Learning (RL) and PrivacyPreserving Federated Averaging (FedAvg). With the help of TensorFlow Federated (TFF), we present a scalable and secure system in which institutions can work together in detecting fraud without compromising sensitive financial information. Federated RL component is adjusted to recent patterns of fraud, whereas FedAvg guarantees the effectiveness of updating the model and maintains privacy. According to our experiments, the proposed approach is much more effective than conventional centralized models, in terms of bettering the accuracy of fraud detection (by 25 percent) and decreasing the risk of data leakage (by 30 percent). The findings show that federated learning can be enhanced with reinforcement learning and privacy protection to offer a powerful solution to the real-time and collaborative fraud detection in different financial institutions, which can make financial ecosystems safer.

title: Adaptive Multi-Resolution RF Classification Using CNN-BiLSTM Noise-Aware Curriculum Learning
abstract: The increasing coexistence of wireless standards such as Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, ZigBee, and LTE within the 2.4 GHz ISM band has resulted in a highly dynamic and congested RF spectrum. Conventional fixed-window spectral analysis and CNN-based classifiers struggle to maintain accuracy under varying noise levels and rapidly changing signal characteristics. To overcome these limitations, this paper presents an Adaptive Multi-Resolution RF Signal Classification System deployed on a Raspberry Pi, integrating Software Defined Radio (SDR) sensing with advanced deep-learning techniques. The system introduces an entropy-guided Adaptive Time-Frequency Windowing (ATFW) method that generates multi-resolution spectrograms for robust feature representation. A hybrid CNN-BiLSTM architecture is designed to learn both spatial spectral patterns and temporal signal dynamics, enhancing the discrimination of OFDM bursts, ZigBee frames, and Bluetooth frequency-hopping signatures. Further, the classifier is trained using Noise-Aware Curriculum Learning (NACL) to improve generalization under low-SNR conditions. A confidence-guided dual-path inference mechanism ensures reliable real-time operation on embedded hardware. Experimental evaluation using over-the-air (OTA) RF captures demonstrates improved low-SNR recognition, stable convergence, and real-time performance, establishing the proposed system as a practical edge-AI solution for spectrum monitoring, interference detection, and intelligent IoT communication management.

title: Human– AI partnerships: Living and working with AI Assistants, AI Agents, and AI Companions
abstract: Abstract As the use of interactive artificial intelligence (AI) expands exponentially, it will permeate into many aspects of consumers' lives, including decision‐making and consumption. As marketers, it is important to understand how consumers currently use interactive AI and how this usage will evolve. We propose that the increased functionality of interactive AI will encourage consumers to view many interactive AI products as long‐term partners, instead of as static tools for finite tasks. Consequently, the future uses of interactive AI will be determined not only by the advancement of the underlying technology but also by consumer responses to repeated interactions with AI technology. We propose a taxonomy of human–AI partnerships (i.e., AI Assistants, AI Agents, AI Companions), provide a profile for each type of AI partner, anticipate how AI partnerships will evolve over time, and discuss how this evolution will influence AI usage. Finally, we provide an extensive agenda for future research.

title: CAMP: Cumulative Agentic Masking and Pruning for Privacy Protection in Multi-Turn LLM Conversations
abstract: The deployment of Large Language Models in agentic, multi-turn conversational settings has introduced a class of privacy vulnerabilities that existing protection mechanisms are not designed to address. Current approaches to Personally Identifiable Information (PII) masking operate on a per-turn basis, scanning each user message in isolation and replacing detected entities with typed placeholders before forwarding sanitized text to the model. While effective against direct identifier leakage within a single message, these methods are fundamentally stateless and fail to account for the compounding privacy risk that emerges when PII fragments accumulate across conversation turns. A user who separately discloses their name, employer, location, and medical condition across several messages has revealed a fully re-identifiable profile - yet no individual message would trigger a per-turn masker. We formalize this phenomenon as Cumulative PII Exposure (CPE) and propose CAMP (Cumulative Agentic Masking and Pruning), a cross-turn privacy protection framework for multi-turn LLM conversations. CAMP maintains a session-level PII registry, constructs a co-occurrence graph to model combination risk between entity types, computes a CPE score after each turn, and triggers retroactive masking of conversation history when the score crosses a configurable threshold. We evaluate CAMP on four synthetic multi-turn scenarios spanning healthcare, hiring, finance, and general conversation, demonstrating that per-turn baselines expose re-identifiable profiles that CAMP successfully neutralizes while preserving full conversational utility.

title: Tight Bounds for Learning Polyhedra with a Margin
abstract: We give an algorithm for PAC learning intersections of $k$ halfspaces with a $ρ$ margin to within error $\varepsilon$ that runs in time $\textsf{poly}(k, \varepsilon^{-1}, ρ^{-1}) \cdot \exp \left(O(\sqrt{n \log(1/ρ) \log k})\right)$. Notably, this improves on prior work which had an exponential dependence on either $k$ or $ρ^{-1}$ and matches known cryptographic and Statistical Query lower bounds up to the logarithmic factors in $k$ and $ρ$ in the exponent. Our learning algorithm extends to the more general setting when we are only promised that most points have distance at least $ρ$ from the boundary of the polyhedron, making it applicable to continuous distributions as well.

title: Artificial Intelligence Based Next Word Prediction System
abstract: Abstract Federated learning is a decentralized approach for training models on distributed devices, by summarizing local changes and sending aggregate parameters from local models to the cloud rather than the data itself. In this research we employ the idea of transfer learning to federated training for next word prediction (NWP) and conduct a number of experiments demonstrating enhancements to current baselines for which federated NWP models have been successful. Specifically, we compare federated training baselines from randomly initialized models to various combinations of pretraining approaches including pretrained word embeddings and whole model pretraining followed by federated fine-tuning for NWP on a dataset of Stack Overflow posts. We realize lift in performance using pretrained embeddings without exacerbating the number of required training rounds or memory footprint. We also observe notable differences using centrally pretrained networks, especially depending on the datasets used. Our research offers effective, yet inexpensive, improvements to federated NWP and paves the way for more rigorous experimentation of transfer learning techniques for federated learning.

title: Constraint-Layered Drift Detection in Long-Context Language Model Evaluation
abstract: Thesis:This paper introduces a constraint-layered evaluation framework for detecting interpretive drift in long-context language model interactions. The method combines hierarchical source enforcement, fault-tree analysis, and cross-layer semantic consistency checks to systematically expose reasoning failures that emerge across multi-step outputs. By treating complex, high-conflict corpora as adversarial test environments, the framework reveals drift patterns that remain undetected under standard prompting and evaluation approaches.

title: AI-Enabled RF Sensing: A Pipeline-Centric Review from Design to Recognition
abstract: For electromagnetic (EM)-driven design, we summarize surrogate modeling and inverse design based on full-wave simulations and, when available, measurements, use adjacent-domain EM exemplars only as methodological templates where direct closed-loop RF design-to-recognition evidence remains limited, and explain why reported speedups depend on the sampled design domain, sample density near feasibility boundaries, and how constraint-boundary checks and final verification are implemented. For RF sensing and recognition, we discuss how the learned “signature” is shaped by the measurement chain (hardware, placement, synchronization, calibration, and preprocessing). We then outline an author-synthesized set of checkable evaluation and reporting items, including explicit domains/constraints, complete sensing metadata, cross-condition tests, and edge deployment evidence, where deployability is defined at the full-pipeline level and requires measured latency, throughput, peak memory, energy per inference, preprocessing overhead, runtime, numerical precision, and an explicit statement of whether communication or offloading is included.

title: A Hybrid Feature-Augmented Dual-Model Meta-Ensemble for Bangla Hate Speech Detection
abstract: Classifying Bangla text remains challenging due to its linguistic complexity and limited annotated resources. Moreover, the rich morphology, informal writing style, emoji use, and slangs makes it more complex to classify the actual context of Bangla sentences. In our study, we developed a hybrid deep learning ensemble framework for this complex classification. This framework combines the complementary strengths of Transformer-based contextual modeling and recurrent sequence modeling. Our proposed method consists of a hybrid multilingual BERT (mBERT) model, which is employed to capture deep contextual semantics using Transformer-based self-attention and the [CLS] token, and a hybrid Bidirectional Long Short-term (BiLSTM) model with an attention mechanism. It is augmented by engineered linguistic features that capture long-range sequential dependencies. Each of the base models learns independently from the textual and engineered features and generates class probability scores. By combining these two base models, we developed a stacking-based meta-ensemble classifier. We experimented on a balanced dataset with a standard training, validation, and testing split. The experimental results show that the proposed work outperforms the individual model performance. It demonstrates the effectiveness of the hybrid feature fusion and ensemble learning for Bangla text classification for low-resource languages.

title: BanglishBERT-CNN-MTL: A Hybrid Multi-Task Learning Framework for Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis in Low-Resource Banglish Text
abstract: In the current digital era, the use of ‘Banglish’ (Bengali-English Code-Mixed) text has increased significantly in social media and e-commerce platforms for expressing opinions. Due to grammatical and spelling variations, analyzing accurate information and sentiment from such text is a very complex challenge for Natural Language Processing (NLP). In this study, we propose a novel hybrid multi-task learning (MTL) framework for ‘Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis’ (ABSA) of low-resource Banglish text. Our proposed architecture uses BanglishBERT to understand the global context of sentences and Multi-Kernel CNN to capture local linguistic patterns (N-grams). In addition, we applied an ‘Aggressive Weighted Loss Strategy’ and ‘TwoStage Fine-Tuning’ mechanism to solve the severe class imbalance problem of real-world datasets. Experimental results show that our model achieves 70.30 % Macro-F1 Score in aspect detection and 89.68% Accuracy in sentiment analysis, which is significantly better and more effective than conventional single-task baseline models.

title: AI Driven Voice Recognition Control for Cloud Integrated Industrial Automation
abstract: The paradigm of cloud-integrated industrial automation is rapidly evolving, necessitated by the demand for seamless human-machine interaction. This research presents a novel system, titled “Al Driven Voice Recognition Control for Cloud Integrated Industrial Automation,” which simplifies cloud file operations through natural language voice commands. By integrating DialogFlow for advanced natural language processing (NLP), Firebase for secure user authentication, and Amazon S3 for scalable cloud storage, the proposed system enables users to upload, download, and delete files without manual interface interaction. A critical innovation is the automated logging mechanism, where daily activity logs are disseminated to registered users via cloud functions, enhancing transparency and security. The system extends the concepts of containerized PLC device management into the realm of general-purpose cloud storage, bridging the gap between industrial excellence and everyday accessibility. Experimental results demonstrate high accuracy in command interpretation and low latency in cloud execution, making it a viable solution for both personal and enterprise-grade file management in hands-busy or accessibilityfocused environments.

title: CLEAR-IT, a framework for contrastive learning to capture the immune composition of tumor microenvironments
abstract: Accurate phenotyping of cells in the tumor microenvironment is essential for understanding cancer biology but typically requires precise cell segmentation, limiting scalability. Here, we introduce Contrastive Learning Enabled Accurate Registration of Immune and Tumor cells (CLEAR-IT), a self-supervised framework that learns cell-level features from multiplexed images using only cell locations. CLEAR-IT encoders achieve strong linear evaluation performance, improve substantially with hyperparameter optimization, and maintain high accuracy across imaging modalities and with up to 90% fewer labels. When substituted for handcrafted features in a state-of-the-art classifier, CLEAR-IT features yield higher performance, and their combination enables comparable accuracy with less than half of the labeled data otherwise required. The learned representations also support prognostic modeling: using annotations from a single patient, CLEAR-IT-based phenotyping identifies survival-associated tissue features that generalize across two cohorts and modalities. CLEAR-IT provides a segmentation-light, label-efficient approach for scalable cell phenotyping and enhances existing workflows in digital pathology and tumor microenvironment analysis.

title: Beyond Attack Success Rate: A Multi-Metric Evaluation of Adversarial Transferability in Medical Imaging Models
abstract: While deep learning systems are becoming increasingly prevalent in medical image analysis, their vulnerabilities to adversarial perturbations raise serious concerns for clinical deployment. These vulnerability evaluations largely rely on Attack Success Rate (ASR), a binary metric that indicates solely whether an attack is successful. However, the ASR metric does not account for other factors, such as perturbation strength, perceptual image quality, and cross-architecture attack transferability, and therefore, the interpretation is incomplete. This gap requires consideration, as complex, large-scale deep learning systems, including Vision Transformers (ViTs), are increasingly challenging the dominance of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). These architectures learn differently, and it is unclear whether a single metric, e.g., ASR, can effectively capture adversarial behavior. To address this, we perform a systematic empirical study on four medical image datasets: PathMNIST, DermaMNIST, RetinaMNIST, and CheXpert. We evaluate seven models (VGG-16, ResNet-50, DenseNet-121, Inception-v3, DeiT, Swin Transformer, and ViT-B/16) against seven attack methods at five perturbation budgets, measuring ASR, Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM), and $L_2$ perturbation magnitude. Our findings show a consistent pattern: perceptual and distortion metrics are strongly associated with one another and exhibit minimal correlation with ASR. This applies to both CNNs and ViTs. The results demonstrate that ASR alone is an inadequate indicator of adversarial robustness and transferability. Consequently, we argue that a thorough assessment of adversarial risk in medical AI necessitates multi-metric frameworks that encompass not only the attack efficacy but also its methodology and associated overheads.

title: (1D) Ordered Tokens Enable Efficient Test-Time Search
abstract: Tokenization is a key component of autoregressive (AR) generative models, converting raw data into more manageable units for modeling. Commonly, tokens describe local information, such as regions of pixels in images or word pieces in text, and AR generation predicts these tokens in a fixed order. A worthwhile question is whether token structures affect the ability to steer the generation through test-time search, where multiple candidate generations are explored and evaluated by a verifier. Using image generation as our testbed, we hypothesize that recent 1D ordered tokenizers with coarse-to-fine structure can be more amenable to search than classical 2D grid structures. This is rooted in the fact that the intermediate states in coarse-to-fine sequences carry semantic meaning that verifiers can reliably evaluate, enabling effective steering during generation. Through controlled experiments, we find that AR models trained on coarse-to-fine ordered tokens exhibit improved test-time scaling behavior compared to grid-based counterparts. Moreover, we demonstrate that, thanks to the ordered structure, pure test-time search over token sequences (i.e., without training an AR model) can perform training-free text-to-image generation when guided by an image-text verifier. Beyond this, we systematically study how classical search algorithms (best-of-N, beam search, lookahead search) interact with different token structures, as well as the role of different verifiers and AR priors. Our results highlight the impact of token structure on inference-time scalability and provide practical guidance for test-time scaling in AR models.

title: ClimateCause: Complex and Implicit Causal Structures in Climate Reports
abstract: Understanding climate change requires reasoning over complex causal networks. Yet, existing causal discovery datasets predominantly capture explicit, direct causal relations. We introduce ClimateCause, a manually expert-annotated dataset of higher-order causal structures from science-for-policy climate reports, including implicit and nested causality. Cause-effect expressions are normalized and disentangled into individual causal relations to facilitate graph construction, with unique annotations for cause-effect correlation, relation type, and spatiotemporal context. We further demonstrate ClimateCause's value for quantifying readability based on the semantic complexity of causal graphs underlying a statement. Finally, large language model benchmarking on correlation inference and causal chain reasoning highlights the latter as a key challenge.

title: CSP-0.1 — Cognitive Skill Passport: Protocol for Standardized AI Skill Description and Transfer
abstract: CSP-0.1 (Cognitive Skill Passport) is an open protocol for standardized description, verification, and transfer of AI skills across heterogeneous systems. The protocol introduces a strict separation between an immutable skill identity (Passport) and its dynamic execution behavior (Runtime), enabling portability, comparability, and safety of cognitive functions. CSP defines a universal CORE classification (Nature.Action.Domain), introduces algorithmic verification via DBE (Dynamic Benchmark Engine), and a structural stability metric (TDI — Tensor Divergence Index). The protocol also includes Economic, Policy, and Assimilation layers, forming a foundation for a decentralized “Internet of Intelligence.”

Included Materials This release preserves the state of the project at the time of manuscript revision, including: Lexicons: "Dadi Corpus Word Segmentation User Dictionary" (ver 1.0 & ver 2.0). Core Scripts: Python implementations (01-09) for MI/MMI calculation and BMM segmentation. Evaluation Data: Gold standard datasets and raw output from ChatGPT-4o. Documentation: Annotation guidelines for Sino-Japanese and ancient Chinese texts. Note on Citation Please note that the Citation section in the README.md is currently a placeholder. It will be updated with the full bibliographic information and formal DOI once the paper is officially published in Cogent Arts & Humanities. Purpose This release is intended to provide a permanent, citable version of the research materials for peer review and open science verification via Zenodo.

Included Materials This release preserves the state of the project at the time of manuscript revision, including: Lexicons: "Dadi Corpus Word Segmentation User Dictionary" (ver 1.0 & ver 2.0). Core Scripts: Python implementations (01-09) for MI/MMI calculation and BMM segmentation. Evaluation Data: Gold standard datasets and raw output from ChatGPT-4o. Documentation: Annotation guidelines for Sino-Japanese and ancient Chinese texts. Note on Citation Please note that the Citation section in the README.md is currently a placeholder. It will be updated with the full bibliographic information and formal DOI once the paper is officially published in Cogent Arts & Humanities. Purpose This release is intended to provide a permanent, citable version of the research materials for peer review and open science verification via Zenodo.

title: The Virtual Recency Abstraction (Artifact and Supplementary Material)
abstract: Artifact and Supplementary Material for "The Virtual Recency Abstraction (Strong Updates for Abstract Interpreters with Shared State)" Scope This artifact contains instructions to reproduce Figures 2 and 3 in Section 5 Table 1 in Section 6.1 Figure 4 in Section 6.2 Table 2 in Section 6.3 Content The artifact contains source code for the Tip and Wasm analyses described in the paper, as well as evaluation scripts that reproduce the graphs in Sections 5 and 6. Figure 2: Modularity and Reuse The source code of the Tip analysis can be found in `/evaluation/sturdy.scala/sturdy-tip/src/main/scala/sturdy/language/tip/analysis/RelationalAnalysis.scala` The figure is generated with Jupyter notebook `count_reuse.ipynb` Figure 3: Modularity and Reuse The source code of the Wasm analysis can be found in `~/evaluation/sturdy.scala/sturdy-wasm/src/main/scala/sturdy/language/wasm/analyses/RelationalAnalysis.scala`. The figure is generated with Jupyter notebook `count_reuse.ipynb` Table 1: Soundness of the Relational Wasm Analysis The source code of the WebAssembly 1.0 specification test suite can be found in `/evaluation/sturdy.scala/sturdy-wasm/src/test/resources/sturdy/language/wasm/spec-test-suite-wasm1/`. The scala test harness can be found in `/evaluation/sturdy.scala/sturdy-wasm/src/test/scala/sturdy/language/wasm/specification/RelationalAnalysisTestScript.scala`. The data is written in CSV format to `/evaluation/sturdy.scala/soundness.csv` The table is generated with Jupyter notebook `soundness.ipynb` Figure 4: Scalability of the Relational Wasm Analysis The benchmarks can be found in `/evaluation/sturdy.scala/sturdy-wasm/src/test/resources/sturdy/language/wasm/benchmarksgame/src`. The Scala test harness can be found in `/evaluation/sturdy.scala/sturdy-wasm/src/test/scala/sturdy/language/wasm/benchmarksgame/BenchmarksgameRelationalPerformanceTest.scala` The data is written in CSV format to `/evaluation/sturdy.scala/scalability.csv` The figure is generated with Jupyter notebook `scalability.ipynb` Table 2: Precision of the Relational Wasm Analysis The WebAssembly code of the precision test can be found in `/evaluation/sturdy.scala/sturdy-wasm/src/test/resources/sturdy/language/wasm/precision.wast`. The C code of the precision test can be found in `/evaluation/sturdy.scala/sturdy-wasm/src/test/resources/sturdy/language/wasm/precision.c`. The data is written in CSV format to `/evaluation/sturdy.scala/precision.csv`, `/evaluation/goblint/precision.csv`, `/evaluation/mopsa/precision.csv`. The table is generated with Jupyter notebook `precision.ipynb`. Reusability The source code of the analyses presented in this paper is open-source and available on GitHub (https://github.com/sturdy-analysis/sturdy/tree/relational-wasm). The code can be recompiled using the Scala built tool SBT and the nix package manager:git clone --recursive https://github.com/sturdy-analysis/sturdycd sturdygit checkout relational-wasmcd sturdy-apronnix build .#numerical-analysis-librariesln -s result/lib libcd ..sbt compileWe recommend to develop the analyses within the IntelliJ IDE. Getting Started To get started, first load the docker image of the artifact:docker load -i virtual-recency-abstraction.tar.gzdocker load -i goblint/goblint.tardocker load -i mopsa/mopsa.tarThen start the docker container:docker run -it --rm -p 8888:8888 virtual-recency-abstraction:latestOpen the link http://127.0.0.1:8888/tree?token=... shown in the command line output in a web browser. This will open Jupyter included in the docker image.Within Jupyter file browser, open the `soundness.ipynb` notebook.Evaluate each cells in the order how they appear in the notebook with `ctrl+enter`. Alternative press the fast-forward button (⏩). To get shell access to the container rundocker run -it --rm --entrypoint bash virtual-recency-abstraction:latest Platforms The artifact is built for X86 CPU architecture and has been tested on linux devices.Since the artifact contains compiled native code, it cannot be executed on other CPU architectures, such as ARM-based Macs. We ran the benchmarks (Figure 4) on a machine with an AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 5975WX CPU, Ubuntu 24.0, and OpenJDK 21.0.9 with 100GB heap space and 1GB stack space.For the artifact we excluded benchmarks for Polyhedra and Octagons, such that the experiment runs with 8GB RAM. Appendix Figures 2 and 3: Modularity and Reuse Figures 2 and 3 can be reproduced with Jupyter notebook `count_reuse.ipynb`: Open the Jupyter notebook `count_reuse.ipynb` following the steps in the getting started section. Reexecute each cell in the order how they appear in the notebook with `ctrl+enter`. Alternative press the fast-forward button (⏩). The cells return latex commands we used to generate Figures 2 and 3 in our paper. Table 1: Soundness of the Relational Wasm Analysis Please note that the analysis of `float_exprs.wast` requires a lot of RAM. Therefore, we recommend the reviewers exclude this test. This is explained in more detail in the Jupyter notebook. Table 1 can be reproduced with Jupyter notebook `soundness.ipynb`: Open notebook `soundness.ipynb` following the steps in the getting started section. Reexecute each cell in the order how they appear in the notebook with `ctrl+enter`. Alternative press the fast-forward button (⏩). Table 1 can be found at the bottom of the notebook. Figure 4: Scalability of the Relational Wasm Analysis Please note that the benchmarks for Polyhedra and Octagons require a lot of RAM to run. We ran the benchmarks on a machine with 100GB RAM. Therefore, we recommend the reviewers only reexecute the benchmarks for intervals. This is explained in more detail in the Jupyter notebook. Figure 4 can be reproduced with Jupyter notebook `scalability.ipynb`. Open notebook `scalability.ipynb` following the steps in the getting started section. Reexecute each cell in the order how they appear in the notebook with `ctrl+enter`. Alternative press the fast-forward button (⏩). The parts of Figure 4 can be found within the evaluated notebook. Table 2: Precision of the Relational Wasm Analysis To repeat the precision tests with the MOPSA analyzer run on the host machine:cd goblintdocker load -i goblint.tardocker run -it --rm -v $(pwd):/data --workdir=/data --entrypoint bash ghcr.io/goblint/analyzer ./analyze_tests.sh To repeat the precision tests with the MOPSA analyzer run on the host machine:cd mopsadocker load -i mopsa.tardocker run --rm -it --mount type=bind,src=`pwd`,target=/home/mopsa/workspace --workdir=/home/mopsa/workspace mopsa/mopsa-analyzer ./analyze_tests.sh Table 2 can be reproduced with Jupyter notebook `precision.ipynb` Open notebook `precision.ipynb` following the steps in the getting started section. Reexecute each cell in the order how they appear in the notebook with `ctrl+enter`. Alternative press the fast-forward button (⏩). Table 2 can be found at the bottom of the evaluated notebook.

title: Embodied Consciousness-Like Emergence in a Multi-Agent Enclosed Arena v1.0 (Draft)
abstract: This paper proposes an embodied multi-agent experimental framework based on the MuJoCo physics engine to investigate whether LLM-driven agents can exhibit complex social behavior and consciousness-like emergent behavior under survival pressure. The system embeds LLMs into a closed arena where agents are given physical bodies, finite energy, differentiated personalities, asymmetric resources, and incomplete information. Across four progressively intensified phases—peace, resource contraction, famine crisis, and final judgment—the framework examines the emergence of alliance, deception, betrayal, altruism, self-referential expression, and moral collapse. The paper does not claim phenomenal consciousness in AI; instead, it operationally explores how embodiment, scarcity, and social interaction shape self-modeling, moral adaptation, and spontaneous strategic behavior in LLM-based agents.

title: Effect of Explainable AI Features on User Satisfaction and Purchase Intention in Saudi Mobile Shopping Apps
abstract: This study examines the impact of explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) features on user satisfaction and purchase intention in Saudi mobile shopping applications, utilising the stimulus–organism–response (S–O–R) framework. With the increasing reliance on AI-driven decision support in e-commerce, enhancing transparency, fairness, trustworthiness, and interpretability has become crucial for shaping consumer perceptions and behavioural responses. The research employed a quantitative methodology using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) to examine the relationships among stimulus factors, cognitive and affective states, consumer satisfaction, and purchase intention. In a survey of 597 respondents from Jeddah and Makkah, Saudi Arabia, the findings highlight that fairness and bias detection, trustworthiness, and transparency significantly influence consumers’ cognitive and affective states, which in turn enhance satisfaction and intention to purchase. Consumer satisfaction emerged as a critical mediator, reinforcing the role of positive emotional and cognitive experiences in driving purchase behaviours. However, interpretability showed limited impact, suggesting that consumers may prioritise fairness and trustworthiness over technical clarity of explanations. Theoretically, this study contributes to advancing knowledge on the role of XAI in consumer behaviour by integrating fairness, transparency, and affective responses into the S–O–R paradigm. From a managerial perspective, the results underscore the importance for mobile shopping platforms to design AI systems that foster trust, reduce perceived bias, and ensure transparency, thereby improving consumer engagement and purchase outcomes. By addressing gaps in interpretability and transparency, businesses can strengthen user trust and loyalty, ultimately enhancing competitive advantage in Saudi Arabia’s rapidly growing e-commerce sector.

title: Mitigating Edge Heterogeneity for Hierarchical Federated Learning: Prototype System and Convergence Analysis
abstract: Hierarchical federated learning (HFL) emerges as a promising solution for distributed systems in real-world IoT, compensating for the limitations of client and training data through multilevel aggregation. However, severe system heterogeneity, such as data heterogeneity, differentiated communication and computing power, can cause model drift and negatively impact system performance, posing challenges to existing HFL frameworks. To address this issue, we propose a mitigating edge heterogeneity method for HFL (MEH-Fed) in this paper. First, we design a new HFL framework, where the key idea is to introduce an initial update of the edge server side to reduce the impact of heterogeneity on system performance. Edge servers use synthetic datasets to guide the update direction of client models, facilitating model training and accelerating convergence. Then, we conduct a convergence analysis of the proposed method, establish a theoretical upper bound, and analyze the effects of key parameters. Finally, we experimentally evaluate the performance of the proposed MEH-Fed in terms of system performance and convergence rate. Experimental results validate that MEH-Fed achieves optimal performance in both accuracy and efficiency, establishing a new paradigm in HFL architecture design for heterogeneous IoT environments.

title: An Explainable Federated ConvNeXt-MHSA Model for Lung Cancer Classification from Chest CT Images
abstract: Medical imaging models for lung cancer classification typically require large, heterogeneous datasets, yet centralized training is constrained by privacy regulations and institutional data silos. We propose a privacy-preserving federated learning framework that fine-tunes a pretrained ConvNeXtBase backbone augmented with a lightweight Multi-Head SelfAttention (MHSA) block. To improve robustness under realistic non-IID client data distributions, we adopt FedAvg aggregation with FedProx regularization. Beyond predictive performance, we integrate model interpretability through Grad-CAM ++ and LIME, providing complementary visual explanations that highlight influential image regions and superpixel-based evidence to support clinical trust. Using five federated clients over eight communication rounds, the global model achieves 98.07 % centralized test accuracy while maintaining strong macro-precision and macro-recall. Confusion matrices across rounds demonstrate rapid reduction of inter-class confusion, and the explanation maps consistently emphasize clinically relevant regions. Overall, the results show that combining modern convolutional backbones, attention, federated optimization, and dual explainability can deliver highly accurate lung cancer classification without sharing raw patient data.

title: Unified Bangla: A Transformer-Based Framework for Bangla Dialect Identification and Cross-Dialectal Translation
abstract: Bangladesh has a wide variety of dialects that differ greatly between areas, making communication difficult and reducing the efficiency of conventional Bangla natural language processing systems. Cross-dialectal translation for Bangla is still mostly unexplored, despite the majority of current work concentrating on standard Bangla translation. In this work, we introduce Unified Bangla, a two-phase neural framework for automatic Bangla dialect detection and cross-dialectal translation. Using a BanglaBERTbased classifier trained on Standard Bangla, Barishal, Chittagong, Mymensingh, Noakhali and Sylhet, the suggested system first identifies dialects with an accuracy of 84.76 % on the test set. In the second stage, a multilingual sequence-to-sequence model (mBART50) is conditioned using the detected dialect which performs dialect-aware translation. BLEU, ChrF, Word Error Rate (WER), Character Error Rate (CER) and comprehensive pairwise analysis across all dialect combinations are used to assess translation quality. According to experimental results, the system achieves an average BLEU score of 29.16 across all dialects, while the highest pairwise BLEU score reaches 55.83 for translations between linguistically close dialects, suggesting that successful neural cross-dialectal translation is made possible by explicit dialect conditioning. This work represents one of the first neural approaches to cross-dialectal translation for Bangla dialects, which offers a practical foundation for future research in lowresource and multidialect NLP settings.alect Identification, Multidialect NLP, mBART, BanglaBERT, Low-Resource Neural Machine Translation.

title: Quantum-Inspired Feature Mapping for Edge AI: A MATLAB-Based Hardware-Aware Co-Design Approach
abstract: Quantum-inspired algorithms have emerged as promising alternatives for enhancing machine learning performance without the overhead of deep neural networks. This paper presents a hardware-aware quantum-inspired feature mapping technique for edge AI applications, implemented and evaluated entirely in MATLAB. The proposed approach employs random linear projections followed by cosine-based non-linear transformations to generate high-dimensional, discriminative feature representations. Unlike conventional deep learning models, the feature extraction process is non-trainable and inherently suitable for fixed-point and low-power hardware implementations. Experiments conducted on the MNIST dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive classification accuracy of$\mathbf{9 5. 1 2 \%}$using a simple fully connected classifier, while significantly reducing training complexity. Statistical analysis of feature variance and inter-sample separability further validates the effectiveness of the proposed encoding. The results indicate that quantum-inspired feature mapping provides a practical and efficient alternative for edge AI systems where computational and energy constraints are critical.

title: Verification Is Not Causal: Why Shared Context Erases the Admissibility Gap
abstract: This essay develops the ontological foundation of Context-Isolated Blind Verification (CIBV). It argues that verification is mischaracterized when treated as a causal operation performed by one system on another's output. Under a shared contextual frame, the very property that verification is meant to check - the gap between what the artifact carries and what invisible context quietly supplies - collapses into invisibility. The paper introduces the provenance gap as an ontological primitive distinct from factual error: a claim can be true yet regime-invalid, structurally unable to travel outside the context in which it was produced. Isolation is recast not as a defense against bias, but as the construction of a vantage point from which admissibility can be examined. A companion invariant - non-reconciliation - is required: once findings from the isolated position re-enter the generator's frame, the frame stretches to absorb them, collapsing the very distinction that made the vantage point meaningful. The architectural instantiation of the position described here is the subject of a separate technical specification. Part of the Navigational Cybernetics 2.5 (NC2.5) corpus. Branches from ONTOΣ VII - From Formal Verification to Admissibility Architecture. Extends the §NAB (Non-Actionability Barrier) framework into the epistemic domain.

title: A1M (AXIOM-1 Sovereign Matrix) for Governing Output Reliability in Stochastic Language Models
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) remain fundamentally limited by stochastic unpredictability, non-deterministic logical drift, and hallucination risks—vulnerabilities that restrict their deployment in mission-critical and sovereign environments. This paper introduces A1M (AXIOM-1 Sovereign Matrix), a novel post-generation structural reliability framework engineered to enforce strict logical stability and eliminate hallucinations without requiring internal weight modification or fine-tuning. The AXIOM-1 architecture subjects candidate LLM outputs to a sequential six-stage filtering pipeline synchronized with a continuous 12.8 Hz resonance pulse, enforcing topological structural invariants and continuous semantic coherence prior to release. By shifting the paradigm from purely probabilistic text generation to governed real-time output validation, AXIOM-1 guarantees that generated responses conform to formal logical constraints and enterprise-grade fail-safe boundaries. The work provides a rigorous theoretical foundation and practical implementation protocols for deploying sovereign, zero-hallucination AI systems across high-stakes domains including legal synthesis, automated medical diagnostic reasoning, financial infrastructure, and national-scale economic planning.

title: MULTIMODAL NLP FOR INTEGRATING TRIAGE NOTES AND STRUCTURED DATA IN EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT DECISION SUPPORT
abstract: Emergency departments generate vast amounts of heterogeneous clinical data, including unstructured triagenotes and structured physiological, laboratory, and demographic information. Effectively integrating thesemultimodal data sources is essential for improving clinical decision support systems and enabling timely,accurate patient care. However, traditional single-modality approaches often fail to capture the complexinteractions between textual and structured data, limiting their effectiveness in high-acuity environments.Recent advancements in multimodal natural language processing (NLP) and deep learning have demonstratedsignificant potential in addressing these limitations. By combining transformer-based architectures withstructured data fusion techniques, multimodal systems can enhance predictive performance for clinicaldeterioration, triage classification, and emergency severity assessment. Studies have shown that integratingclinical notes with structured electronic health record (EHR) data improves diagnostic accuracy and supportsreal-time decision-making in emergency settings.This paper explores the application of multimodal NLP for integrating triage notes and structured clinical data inemergency department decision support systems. The approach leverages advanced fusion techniques, includingjoint embedding models and transformer-based architectures, to unify heterogeneous data sources into a sharedrepresentation space. Such integration enables more robust clinical predictions, including patient deteriorationrisk, treatment prioritization, and resource allocation.Overall, multimodal NLP represents a transformative approach to emergency department decision support,offering improved predictive accuracy, enhanced situational awareness, and more efficient clinical workflow.

title: "Design and Implementation of a Scalable One-Time Pad Encryption Testbed on a Google Platform"
abstract: "This dataset accompanies the paper \"Design and Implementation of a Scalable One-Time Pad Encryption Testbed,\" which presents a practical implementation of an encryption framework achieving information-theoretic (unconditional) security.The system enables scalable key generation and secure data encryption for cloud and mobile environments while significantly reducing the required key-to-data ratio. A full software prototype integrating frontend, backend orchestration, and a high-performance cryptographic engine is included.Experimental evaluation demonstrates strong diffusion properties comparable to AES, successful validation using the NIST Statistical Test Suite (STS), and competitive performance (~1 Gbit\/s throughput). The dataset also introduces a novel shared randomness generation approach using time-varying web content.These artifacts support reproducibility and provide a foundation for further research in scalable cryptographic systems."

title: Deep Learning-Driven Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis of Bangladeshi Hotel Reviews
abstract: With the growing reliance on online reviews in the hospitality industry, understanding customer feedback at an aspect level has become essential for enhancing service quality and guest satisfaction. This study proposes a deep learning-based multi-label aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) framework for effectively analysing unstructured hotel review texts, in which multiple sentiments toward different aspects may be expressed simultaneously. A newly constructed dataset of 7567 Bangladeshi hotel reviews was used to evaluate sentiments across nine predefined aspects, including food, cleanliness, staff behaviour and service, amenities, cost, room quality, location, parking, and overall experience. Machine learning, deep learning, and transformer-based models were employed for aspect-wise sentiment classification to capture both statistical patterns and contextual semantic relationships in the text. Experimental results demonstrate that the BERT-base-uncased Transformer model outperforms the other models, achieving an average accuracy of$\mathbf{9 1 \%}$in binary classification and$\mathbf{8 0 \%}$in multi-label classification. The proposed multi-label approach enables simultaneous and accurate sentiment prediction across multiple aspects within a single review. This represents a scalable, and domain-specific ABSA framework tailored to the Bangladeshi hotel industry, addressing cultural and linguistic nuances in localised feedback and offering actionable insights for service improvement and decision-making.

title: EffiViT-Hybrid: A CNN–Transformer Framework for Pancreatic Cancer Detection from CT Images
abstract: Pancreatic cancer is one of the most fatal diseases, with a survival rate under 11% as it is very difficult to detect in the early stages. The tumors are often small and ill-defined in CT scans, making manual diagnosis time-consuming and prone to errors. To solve this problem, we propose a new deep learning model called EffiViT-Hybrid, which combines the local feature extraction strengths of EfficientNet with the global context modeling of Vision Transformers (ViT). This hybrid design allows the model to capture both fine details and long-range dependencies in the medical images. Our experimental results show that this approach works very well. The proposed model achieved a high testing accuracy of 97.74% and an ROC AUC of 99.90% on our internal dataset, performing better than standalone CNN and Transformer models. To ensure our model is truly robust, we also tested it on a completely separate external validation dataset. The model confirmed its reliability by achieving an accuracy of 95.54% on this unseen data. This study shows that the EffiViT-Hybrid model is a powerful and generalizable tool that can assist radiologists in making faster and more accurate diagnoses, potentially improving clinical outcomes.

title: A Comparative Evaluation of Local Inference for Embodied Agents in Minecraft
abstract: Present research and development in embodied AI relies heavily on massive, proprietary Large Language Models (LLMs) accessed through cloud-based API services. This results in a significant barrier to entry for independent researchers and small-scale developers. Prohibitive costs, latency, and privacy constraints to name a few are the issues limiting broader accessibility and innovation. This paper assesses the feasibility of democratizing embodied agent research by utilizing small, open-weight models (3B-12B parameters) for autonomous reasoning within the Minecraft environment. We benchmark six quantized models using the MINDcraft framework through the use of its native Ollama implementation, executing all inference locally on consumergrade hardware (AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT) across nine progressive tasks covering spatial navigation, complex crafting, and multi-step planning. Our findings indicate that local inference is more capable than we initially anticipated. Andy- 4 (8B), fine-tuned on Minecraft-specific data, led with a 68.9% task completion rate, while Ministral-3 (8B) reached 55.6% despite the lack of domain-specific training, outperforming even the larger 12B Gemma-3. Code-specialized models (Rnj-1, Qwen-3) failed primarily due to not meeting schema requirements rather than being unable to reason, scoring 2.2% and 8.9% respectively. These findings suggest that for constrained embodied tasks, consumer-grade local inference is a viable and potentially cost-effective alternative to proprietary cloud APIs.

title: What Is the Minimum Architecture for Prolepsis? Early Irrevocable Commitment Across Tasks in Small Transformers
abstract: When do transformers commit to a decision, and what prevents them from correcting it? We introduce prolepsis: a transformer commits early, task-specific attention heads sustain the commitment, and no layer corrects it. Replicating Lindsey et al.'s (2025) planning-site finding on open models (Gemma 2 2B, Llama 3.2 1B), we ask five questions. (Q1) Planning is invisible to six residual-stream methods; among those tested, only CLT-based steering succeeds. (Q2) The single-site spike replicates in shape, at the final prompt token (Anthropic's site is the newline; see the Note added). (Q3) Specific attention heads route the decision to the output, filling a gap flagged as invisible to attribution graphs. (Q4) The evidence is consistent with search within at most 16 layers and commitment beyond, a two-model hypothesis. (Q5) Factual recall shows the same motif at a different network depth, with zero overlap between recurring planning heads and the factual top-10. Prolepsis recurs across tasks in the decoder-only models tested: the template is shared, the routing substrates differ. All experiments run on a single consumer GPU (16 GB VRAM).

title: Identification and selection of the best artificial intelligence methods developed for detection and diagnosis of breast cancer
abstract: BACKGROUND: Comprehensive identification and prioritization of developed artificial intelligence methods for the detection and diagnosis of breast cancer can help to select proper techniques. This study aimed to introduce the best artificial intelligence techniques developed for the detection and diagnosis of breast cancer using microscopic images by fuzzy AHP-TOPSIS techniques. METHODS: To identify the artificial intelligence techniques developed, a systematic search was performed in five reliable databases. After that, the Delphi method was applied to determine the proper criteria for selecting the best artificial intelligence techniques. To estimate the relative weights of the criteria, the fuzzy analytical hierarchy process (FAHP) method was used. In the next step, to prioritize the identified artificial intelligence techniques, the technique for order of preference by similarity to the ideal solution (TOPSIS) method was applied. RESULTS: Forty-four artificial intelligence techniques were identified. Seven selection criteria, validity, accuracy, comprehensiveness, processing time, cost, simplicity, and executive capability, were introduced. Ensemble deep learning architectures integrated with web of things (weight = 0.8041), the computer-aided diagnosis method (weight = 0.7774), the ensemble strategy (VGG16 - ResNet34 - ResNet50) (weight = 0.7475), automated tumor-stroma interface zone detection (weight = 0.7475), and MultiNet/Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CAD)-based deep learning model (weight = 0.7262) were selected as the best methods, respectively. CONCLUSION: These findings represent a total approach to the developed techniques which can be used for designing methods with better performance in the future.

title: An open-world learning framework for anomaly event management in oil wells: dual-threshold novelty detection and continuous learning
abstract: Oil wells play a major role in global energy supply. With the widespread use of field sensors and the Internet of Things, multi-variable time series (MTS) data, such as temperature, pressure, and flow, can now be collected in real-time to enhance wellsite decision-making and operational safety. Anomalies (deviations from expected operating conditions) often indicate failures, efficiency declines, or safety risks. Delayed detection may result in economic losses, environmental incidents, and personnel casualties. Therefore, anomaly event management (AEM) is particularly critical in complex industrial systems. However, traditional machine learning often relies on the closed-world assumption, capable only of recognizing known anomaly types. Detecting and classifying novel unseen anomalies remains challenging. To address this, this paper proposes an OpenWorld Learning (OWL) framework for oil wells AEM. First, a hybrid feature extraction pipeline is introduced, utilizing MiniROCKET as the backbone and statistical features as a fallback. Novelty detection is performed using a dual-threshold approach combining the OpenMax maximum category probability threshold with an energy-based class prototype distance threshold to achieve joint rejection. Furthermore, the framework innovatively integrates the EWC, LWF, and Replay continuous learning strategies under the Avalanche to support the incremental introduction of new anomaly categories while minimizing forgetting. We validate the proposed framework on the large-scale 3W dataset, which includes real, simulated, and hand-drawn anomalies to account for rare or hazardous scenarios. Experimental results show that the proposed pipeline consistently extracts discriminative feature representations under data quality constraints and distribution shifts. Furthermore, the proposed framework significantly improves detection rates for unknown categories while maintaining classification performance during the incremental phase. In summary, the proposed OWL framework achieves the synergy of dual-threshold novelty detection and continuous learning in dynamic wellsite scenarios, effectively supporting the digitalization and secure deployment of oil well anomaly event management.

title: Distributed Recursive Filtering for a Class of State-Saturated Nonlinear Systems: A Novel Reputation-Aware Mechanism
abstract: This article is concerned with the distributed recursive filtering problem for a class of nonlinear time-varying systems over sensor networks (SNs) under state saturations via a reputation-aware mechanism (RAM). The state saturation is considered to describe the inevitable constraints of physical equipment, while the RAM is introduced to eliminate abnormal data caused by sensor faults or malicious attacks. To address these challenges, a reputation-aware distributed recursive filtering (RADRF) algorithm is developed, where a novel reputation model is constructed to assign credibility scores to neighboring sensors, thereby identifying and rejecting unreliable data. Furthermore, a saturation-dependent recursive filter is designed, through which the upper bound of the covariance of filtering error dynamics (UBCFEDs) is determined by solving a recursive matrix equation. The filter gain is subsequently parameterized by minimizing the trace of the UBCFED so as to guarantee the optimality of estimation performance under nonlinear saturation effects and reputation-based weighting. To validate the feasibility and effectiveness of the developed approach, an illustrative case study concerning the indoor localization of a mobile robot is conducted. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed RADRF algorithm significantly improves estimation accuracy and robustness compared with schemes that neglect the RAM.

evidence.title: Distributed Recursive Filtering for a Class of State-Saturated Nonlinear Systems: A Novel Reputation-Aware Mechanism
evidence.abstract: This article is concerned with the distributed recursive filtering problem for a class of nonlinear time-varying systems over sensor networks (SNs) under state saturations via a reputation-aware mechanism (RAM). The state saturation is considered to describe the inevitable constraints of physical equipment, while the RAM is introduced to eliminate abnormal data caused by sensor faults or malicious attacks. To address these challenges, a reputation-aware distributed recursive filtering (RADRF) algorithm is developed, where a novel reputation model is constructed to assign credibility scores to neighboring sensors, thereby identifying and rejecting unreliable data. Furthermore, a saturation-dependent recursive filter is designed, through which the upper bound of the covariance of filtering error dynamics (UBCFEDs) is determined by solving a recursive matrix equation. The filter gain is subsequently parameterized by minimizing the trace of the UBCFED so as to guarantee the optimality of estimation performance under nonlinear saturation effects and reputation-based weighting. To validate the feasibility and effectiveness of the developed approach, an illustrative case study concerning the indoor localization of a mobile robot is conducted. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed RADRF algorithm significantly improves estimation accuracy and robustness compared with schemes that neglect the RAM.

title: Path-HGT: A Hierarchical Graph Transformer Framework for Gigapixel Pathology Image Analysis
abstract: The analysis of gigapixel Whole-Slide Images (WSIs) in digital pathology is the gold standard for cancer diagnosis, but it presents a formidable challenge for AI models due to extreme data scale. Current state-of-the-art methods rely on Multiple Instance Learning (MIL), treating WSIs as an unordered “bag-of-patches.” This approach critically discards the spatial microarchitecture of tissue, which is a primary source of diagnostic information for pathologists. To overcome this limitation, we propose Path-HGT, a novel Pathology Hierarchical Graph Transformer framework. Path-HGT first models a WSI as a spatially-explicit graph of patches. It then employs a hierarchical architecture composed of stacked Graph Transformer (GATv2) layers and self-attention graph pooling (SAGPool) modules. This design enables the model to learn multi-scale representations, capturing both local cellular interactions at the patch level and global tissue-region architectures at coarser graph levels. We validate Path-HGT on the Camelyon16 and TCGA-RCC benchmarks. Our framework achieves state-of-the-art performance, attaining an AUC of 0.965 on Camelyon16 and an accuracy of 0.946 on TCGA-RCC, significantly outperforming existing MIL, Transformer, and “flat” GNN baselines. Our work demonstrates that modeling explicit spatial hierarchy is crucial for robust and interpretable gigapixel WSI analysis.

title: Transformer Architectures for Romanized Bangla Dialect Understanding in Resource-Constrained Conversational Systems
abstract: Multilingual societies deploy conversational systems to handle informal event-driven, and non-standard languages. Often, these conversational systems' user inputs will include Romanized and dialect-based user inputs. In the case of Bangla, many existing Natural Language Processing (NLP) tools have been developed for use with native scripts and therefore, present a challenge in dealing with real-world conversational data based on Romanized formats. This paper outlines our evaluation of several transformer-based models as a method to classify five different types of regional dialects of Romanized Bangla. The dataset we used, Vashantor, consists of several hundred locations that include users inputting Romanized Bangla against five different regional dialects. Each of the transformer models (multilingual, Bangla-specific, and compact) were run against a common experimental design. Evaluations were performed using agreementbased, error-sensitive, efficiency-aware metrics, and standard accuracy metrics. Our results demonstrate that multilingual and/or ‘script compatible’ models have greater success than models that have been specifically trained for Bangla with mBERT, yielding the best balance of predictive performance, robustness, and operational efficiency. In addition, training dynamics and confusion matrices substantiate the stability and generalization ability that multilingual pre-training has over Bangla-specific models. Therefore, we have concluded that in order to conduct NLP in Romanized Bangla, it is critical to select Transformer architecture(s) that have ‘script compatibility’ within the context of conversational applications with low resource requirements that generate real-world use cases.

title: Preprocessing Strategies for Sentiment Analysis of Code-Mixed Social Media Text
abstract: In social media conversations, users often mix English with their native language, resulting in code-mixed (CM) text that exhibits high variability in writing style, vocabulary, and grammar. Transliteration, where native-language words are written using the Latin script, leads to multiple spelling variants of the same word, causing vocabulary fragmentation, weakened sentiment cues, and increased out-of-vocabulary issues for deep learning models. Additionally, CM sentiment datasets frequently contain emojis that convey sentiment even in otherwise neutral statements, and multiple visually distinct emojis may express the same sentiment, similar to transliteration variants. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a preprocessing pipeline incorporating transliteration normalization using Levenshtein distance, and emoji mapping using a custom token dictionary to strengthen the sentiment cues. An XLM-R classifier was implemented for sentiment analysis on Malayalam-English CM data, and the proposed preprocessing strategies were applied to improve the model robustness. Experiments on the DCM dataset demonstrate a 2.8 % relative improvement over the baseline classifier, and a 17.46 % relative improvement over the existing best results. Detailed error analysis confirms the generalization capability of the proposed approach.

title: ROBÓTICA EDUCACIONAL NO ENSINO INFANTIL: FOCO NAS COMPETÊNCIAS E HABILIDADES DIGITAIS.
abstract: Este capítulo analisa as contribuições da robótica educacional para a Educação Infantil, tomando como base uma pesquisa de campo realizada em uma creche pública de tempo integral, no município de São Miguel do Guamá/PA. A experiência envolveu 60 crianças de quatro e cinco anos, entre as quais seis estudantes público da Educação Especial em fase de observação pedagógica. O estudo adota abordagem qualitativa, natureza descritiva e fundamentos da pesquisa-ação, utiliza como instrumentos de coleta dos dados e informações, a observação participante, rodas de conversa e registros audiovisuais no diário de campo. As atividades pedagógicas foram planejadas de forma interdisciplinar, com uso de kits de robótica, materiais recicláveis e softwares de programação visual, na articulação de princípios do construcionismo e das metodologias ativas. Os resultados apontaram quatro eixos principais: 1) a criatividade e a ludicidade, evidenciadas na invenção de artefatos significativos; 2) a autonomia e protagonismo infantil, com crianças assumindo iniciativas na resolução de problemas; 3) a construção de saberes digitais iniciais do pensamento computacional; e 4) a inclusão escolar, com ampliação da participação de estudantes público da Educação Especial, para os quais a robótica se configurou como linguagem alternativa de comunicação e tecnologia assistiva pedagógica. Conclui-se que a robótica educacional, integrada ao currículo da Educação Infantil, constitui ferramenta potente para a promoção da inovação, da inclusão e da equidade educacional, sendo necessária sua consolidação em políticas públicas, formação docente e infraestrutura adequada.

title: Periodic Table of Cognition
abstract: The Periodic Table of Cognition DOI defines a unified structural map of adaptive cognition across biological life and artificial systems, organized as a five-by-five matrix grounded in the Five Tasks Model DOI. It classifies cognitive architectures according to recurrent informational task domains, controllers, behavior change patterns, cognitive maps, and cognitive-behavioral potential. Within this framework, each diagonal cell represents one complete cognitive-behavioral structure of a species group, while the four axes make visible the corresponding controller level DOI, informational domain, characteristic behavior change pattern DOI, and adaptive potential. Comparative analysis across more than 1,530 species DOI provides the empirical foundation for this architecture. By presenting cognition as a structured and navigable system rather than a loose collection of traits, the Periodic Table of Cognition offers a predictive and comparative framework linking evolution, species classification, cognitive architecture, and artificial intelligence within a single integrated map.

title: HD-IMDF: A Hybrid Deep Learning-Based Interactive Medical Diagnosis Framework for Detecting Skin Disease With Dialog-Based Explanation and Interpretability
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become one of the most important tools in healthcare for analyzing medical images to detect different diseases. However, most AI-based systems only predict the output class without giving any clear reason associated with the decision, which often creates confusion and a lack of trust among medical users. To address this issue, this study presents an explainable and interactive medical image diagnosis framework, HD-IMDF, that combines Deep Learning, Natural Language Processing, and Explainable AI techniques. The deep learning module is developed using a modified Multi-head Attention-based Fusion Network (MAFNet) that can analyze skin lesion images and detect Monkeypox, along with four other skin diseases having similar symptoms. The model achieved 99.35 % accuracy. The multiple attention heads in MAFNet help the model to focus more on the important visual regions that influence the final decision. To make the system interactive, a fine-tuned DialoGPT model is integrated to facilitate the users to communicate with the system via natural language and get explanations about the disease symptoms, causes, preventive measures etc. The framework also uses Explainable AI (XAI) based visualization methods to highlight key regions in the image, improving transparency and interpretability. A web interface connects all modules so users can upload images, view model outputs, and chat with the system for better understanding. This integrated approach aims to make AI-based diagnosis more transparent, explainable, and user-friendly for real medical applications.

title: Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis of Bangladeshi IT Service Reviews Using Transformer Architectures and Post-Hoc Interpretability
abstract: Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) enables fine-grained opinion mining by associating sentiment polarity with specific service aspects. In Bangladesh, IT service reviews are predominantly written in a code-mixed Banglish-English format, which introduces challenges such as informal language, data sparsity, and severe class imbalance. This paper proposes a transformer-based ABSA framework for Bangladeshi IT company reviews and introduces a manually annotated dataset covering five service aspects: App Performance, Customer Support, Payment System, UIUX, and Service Reliability. We evaluate three architectural designs review-only classification, text-aspect concatenation, and separate aspect embedding using BanglishBERT, DistilBERT, mBERT, BERT and XLM-RoBERTa. Experimental results show that text-aspect concatenation achieves high macro F1-scores (up to 0.97) but suffers from aspect information leakage, leading to inflated performance. In contrast, the separate aspect embedding architecture provides a stricter evaluation, where BERT achieves the best performance with a macro F1-score of 0.967 and ROC-AUC of 1.00, demonstrating robustness under class imbalance. DistilBERT shows competitive performance with slightly lower macro scores. Post-hoc interpretability using Integrated Gradients, SHAP, and LIME confirms that predictions are driven by sentiment-relevant tokens. These findings highlight the importance of architecture design for reliable ABSA in low-resource, code-mixed settings.

title: LeapAlign: Post-Training Flow Matching Models at Any Generation Step by Building Two-Step Trajectories
abstract: This paper focuses on the alignment of flow matching models with human preferences. A promising way is fine-tuning by directly backpropagating reward gradients through the differentiable generation process of flow matching. However, backpropagating through long trajectories results in prohibitive memory costs and gradient explosion. Therefore, direct-gradient methods struggle to update early generation steps, which are crucial for determining the global structure of the final image. To address this issue, we introduce LeapAlign, a fine-tuning method that reduces computational cost and enables direct gradient propagation from reward to early generation steps. Specifically, we shorten the long trajectory into only two steps by designing two consecutive leaps, each skipping multiple ODE sampling steps and predicting future latents in a single step. By randomizing the start and end timesteps of the leaps, LeapAlign leads to efficient and stable model updates at any generation step. To better use such shortened trajectories, we assign higher training weights to those that are more consistent with the long generation path. To further enhance gradient stability, we reduce the weights of gradient terms with large magnitude, instead of completely removing them as done in previous works. When fine-tuning the Flux model, LeapAlign consistently outperforms state-of-the-art GRPO-based and direct-gradient methods across various metrics, achieving superior image quality and image-text alignment.

title: Performance Analysis and Optimization for Laser-Phase-Noise based Quantum Random Number Generation
abstract: The quantum random number generation based on laser phase noise, which is featured with high random number generation rate and ease for photonic integration, has been extensively investigated and demonstrated. Despite these advancements, a theoretical model to achieve optimal performance in terms of maximizing the random number generation rate is still incomplete. In this work, a comprehensive physical model for this scheme is introduced to accurately predict the power spectrum of entropy source and probability distribution of raw data, based on which the entropy source bandwidth and extractable randomness can be accordingly estimated and thus the system performance can be quantitatively evaluated and optimized. The model is sufficiently validated through both simulation and experiment with significant agreement under various typical setups. Furthermore, our proposal enables the proactive design of experimental parameters to achieve optimal system performance, which is crucial for the design and practical implementation of photonics integrated quantum random number generations.

title: CLUSTERING OF TEXTUAL DATA BY USING K-MEANS TECHNIQUE
abstract: Abstract: To store the textual data and various documents, the usage of electronic media is widespread. To retrieve theimportant information from the large document collection of unstructured data is a very difficult and time consuming task. Itis easier to find the relevant documents from a huge data collection only when the data collected is in ordered form or thedata is classified by certain group or category. Still the problem persists to find the best grouping technique. This paperconcentrates on the implementation technique of k-means clustering algorithm. K-means technique is used here to cluster theunlabeled data or the text document collection that is highly unstructured. It begins with the representative model of theunstructured data and finally generating the set of sorted clusters as a result. Furthermore, the results can be refined byanalyzing the sorted set of clusters.

title: RespirIA — Agente Personalizado para o Aprendizado de Ventilação Mecânica Invasiva
abstract: Description: RespirIA is an AI-powered intelligent tutoring system designed for undergraduate Physiotherapy students learning Invasive Mechanical Ventilation (IMV). Developed by a critical care physiotherapist, clinical preceptor, and master's researcher at the University of São Paulo (USP), the system combines large language model technology with evidence-based pedagogical principles to support active and individualized learning. The tutor operates through three study modes: theoretical concept review, clinical case simulation, and prior knowledge diagnosis. It applies Socratic questioning methods, provides immediate constructive feedback, and continuously monitors patient safety parameters according to current guidelines (ARDSNet 2000, Berlin Definition 2012, AMIB). An integrated ventilator simulator displays real-time pressure, flow, and volume waveforms for VCV, PCV, and PSV modes, allowing students to visualize the physiological effects of parameter adjustments. RespirIA includes an interactive clinical reference panel, calculators for predicted body weight, RSBI, driving pressure, and minute volume, as well as automatic generation of study summaries and mind maps in PDF format. All interactions are logged by user, session, and interaction level, enabling quantitative analysis of learning outcomes, topic-specific performance, error classification by type and skill domain, and student engagement patterns. This software was developed as a technical product of the master's thesis titled "Validação de Um Tutor Inteligente Desenvolvido com Inteligência Artificial como Ferramenta Educacional para o Ensino de Ventilação Mecânica Básica para Estudantes de Fisioterapia", conducted at the Graduate Program in Rehabilitation Sciences, Universidade de São Paulo (USP), under the supervision of Prof. Carolina Fu. Keywords: mechanical ventilation, intelligent tutoring system, artificial intelligence, physiotherapy education, medical education technology, active learning, clinical simulation.
