title: The Skill Navigator - An AI Driven Personalized Learning and Skill Gap Analyzer
abstract: The Skill Navigator is an AI-driven web application that analyzes users' existing competencies and identifies skill gaps relative to their desired career or learning goals. By leveraging the GROQ-powered LLaMA 3.3-70B language model, the system delivers personalized learning recommendations, an adaptive AI chatbot assistant (BOD – Bot of Development), and an interactive quiz engine. The platform integrates a React.js frontend with a Flask-based REST API backend and Supabase for authentication and profile management. Users receive curated skill paths across categories including Web Development, AI/ML, Cloud Computing, Cybersecurity, and Soft Skills. The system dynamically adapts its recommendations based on user profile data, quiz performance history, and stated learning objectives. The system provides contextual guidance, answers queries, and orchestrates quiz sessions based on conversational intent detection. The system also incorporates a profile management layer backed by Supabase, enabling persistent storage of user goals, interests, and quiz performance history. This paper presents the system architecture, core modules, database design, implementation details, and the outcomes of deploying an AI-personalized learning navigator for modern skill development, demonstrating how modern AI technologies can be harnessed to deliver practical, personalized, and scalable learning solutions.

title: A Speech Driven Framework for Identifying Low Resourced Ethnic Languages of Bangladesh
abstract: The ethnic languages with limited resources are not well represented in the field of computational speech, which makes it challenging to implement into the new technology. This study introduces a speech-based machine-learning system to detect 3 low-resource ethnic languages of Bangladesh that are Chakma, Marma and Garo. A collection of 2,321 audio samples of different native speakers was gathered, reading translated versions of 211 sentences in Bangali. The samples were checked to be linguistically correct and they were normalized in WAV format. Noise, silence, normalization and Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficient (MFCC) extraction were performed as the preprocessing steps to obtain the consistent feature representations that can be used in machine-learning analysis. Through MFCC features, a set of classical machine-learning models, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression, Random Forest and K-Nearest Neighbors, were trained. The accuracy of the SVM and Random Forest models were the highest, with both models obtaining accuracy of 99.35 %, whereas the accuracy of the Logistic Regression and KNN is 99.14 % and 98.92 % respectively. These good findings indicate that classical machine-learning approaches can be used to reasonably well learn the acoustic patterns of the differences between Chakma, Garo, and Marma, even with a relatively small dataset. In order to improve interpretability, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) was used on the SVM and the Random Forest models. SHAP outcome indicated that the most valuable features in all models were mfcc5mean, and the MFCCmean category was the most significant. On the whole, the results support the possibility of constructing an effective and explainable system of language-identification of low-resourced Bangladeshi languages with the help of classical machine learning. The future research consists of dataset expansion, deep-learning implementation, as well as real-time deployment to further digital inclusion and language preservation.

title: RBE-Sent: A Synthetic Roman Bengali-English Code-Mixed Dataset For Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Datasets play a crucial role in natural language processing (NLP), enabling the development and evaluation of various tasks. However, in the Bengali-English code-mixed context, sentiment analysis research faces a major challenge due to the severe scarcity of dataset resources. This work, in this paper, presents RBE-Sent, a new synthetic Roman BengaliEnglish (RBE) code-mixed product review dataset designed for sentiment analysis. The corpus was constructed from English Amazon web shopping reviews with a hybrid method that combined translation, transliteration, and a novel lexicon-based ensemble approach for sentiment tagging. RBE-Sent comprises Bengali-matrix code-mixed reviews and showed benchmark performance for training and testing on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), multilingual Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (mBERT), and Support Vector Machine (SVM) models. The new dataset generation process can similarly be applied to generate other Englishengaged code-mixed resources.

title: Twin Parametric Margin Support Vector Regression Model with Huber Loss Function
abstract: ABSTRACT Although there are some recent methods, such as SVR, TSVR, and TPSVR, that enhance training speed by using nonparallel hyperplanes, they remain sensitive to outliers and non‐Gaussian noise, like the ‐insensitive loss function‐based methods. We propose a method to tackle this issue, namely the Huberized TPSVR framework. This model offers a dual protection mechanism: the parametric margins adapt to the local density in the data, while the integrated Huber loss function guides the learning process through robust noise and extreme outliers. Our experiments on complex chemical and clinical data reveal the remarkable superiority of Huberized TPSVR over standard models in terms of both stability and accuracy, which provides an efficient approach for addressing the messy nature of real‐world multidimensional data.

title: MM-WebAgent: A Hierarchical Multimodal Web Agent for Webpage Generation
abstract: The rapid progress of Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC) tools enables images, videos, and visualizations to be created on demand for webpage design, offering a flexible and increasingly adopted paradigm for modern UI/UX. However, directly integrating such tools into automated webpage generation often leads to style inconsistency and poor global coherence, as elements are generated in isolation. We propose MM-WebAgent, a hierarchical agentic framework for multimodal webpage generation that coordinates AIGC-based element generation through hierarchical planning and iterative self-reflection. MM-WebAgent jointly optimizes global layout, local multimodal content, and their integration, producing coherent and visually consistent webpages. We further introduce a benchmark for multimodal webpage generation and a multi-level evaluation protocol for systematic assessment. Experiments demonstrate that MM-WebAgent outperforms code-generation and agent-based baselines, especially on multimodal element generation and integration. Code & Data: https://aka.ms/mm-webagent.

title: IMPROVING THE EFFICIENCY OF REINFORCEMENT LEARNING ALGORITHMS THROUGH THE INTRODUCTION OF EMPIRICAL RULES
abstract: This paper considers an approach to accelerating and stabilising reinforcement learning (RL) by incorporating empirical rules implemented at the environment level, without modifying the base algorithm. The proposed strategy allows for the termination of known-failure episodes and the adjustment of the agent’s interaction with the environment based on domain constraints. Experiments conducted on the highly complex BipedalWalker-v3 environment demonstrate a more than 50 per cent increase in average reward with comparable training time, confirming the practical significance of the method. The approach is algorithmically general and can be implemented in existing RL systems without structural changes to the optimisation algorithms. Keywords: reinforcement learning, heuristics, reward, agent, strategy.

title: Lung-Attnet: An Attention Mechanism-Based Cnn Architecture For Lung Cancer Detection With Federated Learning
abstract: Lung cancer is one of the most serious threats to human health today and it is responsible for a large proportion of deaths from cancer each year. In order to improve survival rates and provide timely intervention, early and accurate detection of lung cancer is essential. This project proposes a smart lung cancer detection system using deep learning techniques on computed tomography (CT) scan images to automate the detection of lung cancer through the use of an artificial intelligence (AI) based Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model. The CNN model uses automatically learnt complex representations of CT images to extract relevant features and patterns associated with cancerous lung nodules, and this allows the model to identify malignant lung tissues from non-malignant lung tissues with high accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. The dataset for this project consists of publicly available CT images from both lung cancer patients and benign patients. During training, the CNN model learns how to identify the small variations between the patterns of the CT images resulting from lung cancer and the patterns resulting from being benign. The results from extensive experimental analysis demonstrate that the proposed system can reliably detect lung cancer. The use of an automated detection system decreases the reliance on visual inspection by a physician, and subsequently, reduces the occurrence of diagnostic errors. The approach proposed in this study is a non-invasive decision support tool that provides a reliable and efficient way for radiologists to diagnose lung cancer earlier than before and thus enhance the quality of care for patients treated for lung cancer.

title: BAN-SentiFuse: A Feature Fusion Technique for Bangla Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Sentiment analysis of Bangla text has drawn more interest recently because of its numerous applications in assessing popular opinion on digital platforms, social media, and entertainment. In contrast to high-resource languages, Bangla's linguistic complexity and the absence of reliable techniques that can capture its semantic richness have hindered development in this area. This study proposed BAN-SentiFuse, a feature fusion framework for Bangla sentiment classification. The technique constructs 3072-dimensional semantic features by concatenating the [CLS] token outputs from BanglaBERT's final four transformer layers to extract contextual embeddings. These are utilized with TF-IDF vectorized 2000-dimensional statistical representations to create a complete$\mathbf{5 0 7 2}$-dimensional feature space. A multilayer perceptron network (MLP) and popular machine learning classifiers were employed to utilize the fused features. Experimental results on a benchmark dataset of Bangla drama and TV series reviews demonstrate that BAN-SentiFuse frequently surpasses conventional ML approaches and even a deep learning-based stacking ensemble when evaluated on the same dataset. With an F1-score of 0.83 and an accuracy of 83.52%, the MLP classifier demonstrated outstanding performance. These results exhibit how well semantic and statistical characteristics can be combined, providing a strong foundation for sentiment analysis in low-resource languages like Bangla.

title: Understanding Learner Perceptions in Distance Education Using Sentiment Classification
abstract: Distance learning has become a crucial method of education, especially in the period of the COVID-19 pandemic, which also allows learning and teaching to take place outside regular classrooms in both synchronous and asynchronous environments. It is fundamental to ensure an improvement in the effectiveness of this modality by gaining an understanding of the perception of this modality among the population. The work is an analysis using Natural Language Processing (NLP) and machine learning models on a Kaggle dataset of user-created comments expressing their sentiments about distance learning. Sentiment labeling of the comments was done using VADER (Valence Aware Dictionary and sEntiment Reasoner), which groups comments into positive, negative, and neutral. The positive sentiments related to words such as “accessibility” and “flexibility,” whereas words that indicate challenging issues of technology and infrastructure included negative sentiments. A variety of models were tried to compare the sentiment classification, including SVM, logistic regression, CNN, LSTM, BiLSTM, random forest, and BERT. Out of them, BERT established the best accuracy (95%), followed by BiLSTM (94%; and SVM/LSTM (93%). The results reveal that although distance learning is mostly valued because of it's flexibility and it's ability to be inclusive, there is some concern around the limitations of technicality and quality of learning experiences. These observations suggest a good implication for educators, institutions, and policymakers to improve the digital learning systems. In the future, aspect-based sentiment analysis and real-time feedback can be incorporated to enhance the learner.

title: Weighted Federated Distillation: A knowledge-quality-aware, teacher-less strategy
abstract: The rapid advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and edge devices have driven the proliferation of smart-world applications, many of which are deployed in distributed environments. In contexts where data privacy must be maintained, Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a promising privacy-preserving collaborative learning paradigm, offering significant potential to harness the distributed data available at the network’s edge. However, the heterogeneity of devices and the non-Independent and Identically Distributed (IID) nature of data across them pose significant challenges, undermining the performance of FL systems. To address these issues, Knowledge Distillation (KD) has proven to be a valid solution. Initially developed as a teacher-student training paradigm, KD enhances the performance of smaller student networks by transferring knowledge from larger, more powerful teacher networks. When integrated with FL, KD offers additional benefits: it mitigates the effects of data and model heterogeneity and compensates for the absence of a centralized teacher model. This is achieved by creating a global knowledge representation derived from the aggregated knowledge of individual clients. Building on these principles, we propose Weighted-FD, a novel framework that introduces a quality-aware approach to global knowledge computation. Unlike conventional methods, Weighted-FD evaluates the quality of knowledge contributed by each client and dynamically adjusts their influence on the global knowledge representation. This ensures a more accurate and effective aggregation process. We detail the mathematical foundation of our framework and validate its efficacy through extensive experiments conducted on MNIST, FashionMNIST, and CIFAR-10 under different data heterogeneity settings (IID, weak non-IID, and strong non-IID). The results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing federated distillation approaches. In particular, Weighted-FD achieves substantial improvements under strong non-IID conditions, reaching accuracy gains of up to 57.12% over FedMD and 49.34% over Selective-FD on CIFAR-10, while maintaining low computational and memory requirements, making it well suited for deployment in resource-constrained edge environments. The source code for Weighted-FD is publicly available at the following link: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/weighted-fd-C6EC/ .

The source code for Weighted-FD is publicly available at the following link: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/weighted-fd-C6EC/ .

title: Locality, Not Spectral Mixing, Governs Direct Propagation in Distributed Offline Dynamic Programming
abstract: We study the communication complexity of distributed offline dynamic programming, where a fixed batch dataset is partitioned across (M) machines connected by the data-induced dependency graph. We compare two paradigms: direct boundary-value propagation, which follows Bellman dependencies, and gossip averaging, which mixes local estimates. Our results show that **locality** is the fundamental driver of round complexity. In particular, we prove that no method can achieve (\varepsilon)-accuracy in fewer than (L_\varepsilon = \left\lfloor \log(1/2\varepsilon) / \log(1/γ) \right\rfloor) rounds on graphs of diameter at least (L_\varepsilon), and we show that direct propagation matches this scaling up to constants, attaining error (O(γ^T/(1-γ) + δ/(1-γ))) after (T) rounds. In contrast, gossip-style fitted value iteration incurs an additional (1/\mathrm{gap}(W)) dependence in both convergence rate and asymptotic error. We also prove bandwidth-sensitive lower bounds on path topologies and extend the analysis to asynchronous systems with bounded delays. Together, these results show that spectral dependence is an artifact of gossip-based algorithms, whereas locality is the intrinsic barrier in distributed offline dynamic programming.

title: Computing the free energy of quantum Coulomb gases and molecules via quantum Gibbs sampling
abstract: We develop a quantum Gibbs-sampling approach to free-energy estimation for trapped systems of distinguishable particles with Coulomb interactions in dimensions $d\in\{2,3\}$. The singular infinite-dimensional problem is reduced to a finite-rank low-energy truncation of the interaction, the truncated Gibbs state is prepared by a quantum Markov semigroup, and thermodynamic integration gives the free energy. We obtain explicit truncation rates, quantitative spectral-gap estimates, and a finite-dimensional circuit implementation. In particular, every fixed interaction truncation has a positive gap, while weak truncated interactions admit a particle-number-independent lower bound. The circuit complexity is conditional on a certified gap lower bound at the accuracy-dependent interaction cutoff.

title: CAMO: An Agentic Framework for Automated Causal Discovery from Micro Behaviors to Macro Emergence in LLM Agent Simulations
abstract: LLM-empowered agent simulations are increasingly used to study social emergence, yet the micro-to-macro causal mechanisms behind macro outcomes often remain unclear. This is challenging because emergence arises from intertwined agent interactions and meso-level feedback and nonlinearity, making generative mechanisms hard to disentangle. To this end, we introduce \textbf{\textsc{CAMO}}, an automated \textbf{Ca}usal discovery framework from \textbf{M}icr\textbf{o} behaviors to \textbf{M}acr\textbf{o} Emergence in LLM agent simulations. \textsc{CAMO} converts mechanistic hypotheses into computable factors grounded in simulation records and learns a compact causal representation centered on an emergent target $Y$. \textsc{CAMO} outputs a computable Markov boundary and a minimal upstream explanatory subgraph, yielding interpretable causal chains and actionable intervention levers. It also uses simulator-internal counterfactual probing to orient ambiguous edges and revise hypotheses when evidence contradicts the current view. Experiments across four emergent settings demonstrate the promise of \textsc{CAMO}.

title: Communication Complexity of Lattice-Based Cryptographic Protocols: First Exact Bounds for LWE-CC and a New Multiparty Problem from Quorum Key Recovery
abstract: We initiate the study of communication complexity (CC) for Learning With Errors (LWE) based cryptographic protocols — the mathematical core of the NIST post-quantum standards ML-KEM (FIPS 203) and ML-DSA (FIPS 204). We define the LWE Communication Problem (LWE-CC ): Alice holds secret s ∈ Zn and error vector e; Bob holds matrix A ∈ Zm×n; nqq their joint goal is for Bob to compute b = As + e (mod q) via one-way communication. We make four contributions. First, we prove the lower bound CC(LWE-CCn) ≥ n log2 q bits rigorously. Second, we compute the rank of the communication matrix Mf , fooling set sizes, and discrepancy bounds exactly for small parameters via exhaustive enumeration, producing numbers that do not appear in any prior work: rank(Mf ) ∈ {31, 53, 126} and fooling sets of size ≥ {104, 114, 173} for (n, q) ∈ {(2, 5), (2, 7), (3, 5)}. Third, we observe the empirical pattern rank(Mf ) ≈ qn and state it as Conjecture 1. Fourth, we analyze the hard distribution μ∗ via a coordinate-descent LP, finding it concentrates on zero-secret inputs (s = 0) — a regime that reduces to the INDEX function with no quantum advantage — and conclude the quantum-classical separation must lie in the s ̸= 0 regime where the VSP geometry is active. We also define QV-CCN,k, a new multiparty quantum CC problem derived from the quorum vault recovery protocol of QuantumMail-v2, and prove its classical complexity is Θ(k log p). To our knowledge this is the first CC analysis of any deployed NIST PQC standard operation, and the first formulation of threshold key recovery as a multiparty communication complexity problem.

title: Strategic Approach for Enhancing Deep Learning Models
abstract: Modern large language models have achieved remarkable growth and performance across domains, yet their intense use of resources and high computational costs present challenges to scalability and sustainability. Current attempts to surpass baseline (naïve) AutoDL (Automated Deep Learning) models often rely on complex manipulations to yield marginal accuracy gains while demanding deep domain knowledge and computational intensity. To address known inefficiencies in computation and implementation, this study proposes a strategic approach for enhancing processing without compromising model accuracy or performance through a simplified, scalable methodology. We present a novel AutoDL weight optimization model method that analyzes the most accurate deep learning starting point and achieves the highest outcomes while considering the additional “presetting” analysis overhead. Using 20 real-world datasets, we conducted experiments across three models, six weight configurations, and ten seeds, totaling 62,400 epochs. In all experiments, the optimized model outperformed baselines, achieving higher accuracy across every dataset while reducing preprocessing to only two epochs per seed. These results demonstrate that minimal preprocessing—limited to two epochs per seed—can substantially lower computational demand while maintaining precision. As the global demand for AI deployment accelerates, this conservation-oriented approach will be critical to sustaining innovation within resource and infrastructural constraints, enabling advances in computational sustainability and responsible AI development, tangible savings across multiple dimensions of resource consumption, and broader access to deep learning technologies.

title: "NASA SOLAR irradiance and temperature data"
abstract: "This dataset contains hourly solar irradiance and temperature data obtained from the NASA POWER database for a specific geographic location. It includes measured and model-derived parameters, namely predicted solar irradiance and corresponding photovoltaic (PV) power output. The predictions are generated using data-driven modeling techniques to support renewable energy forecasting and microgrid energy management studies. The dataset is structured for time-series analysis and is suitable for applications in solar forecasting, intelligent energy management, and digital twin-based optimization of energy systems. It enables the evaluation of machine learning models and advanced control strategies for improving the performance and reliability of solar-integrated power system"

title: FedKD: A Fine-Grained Parameter-Efficient Federated Co-Tuning Framework With Knowledge Decoupling for Large and Small Foundation Models
abstract: Recently, federated foundation models (FedFM) have emerged as a promising approach. FedFM preserves data privacy while co-tuning foundation models (FM) across edge nodes. However, the high complexity and numerous parameters of FM hinder the deployment across diverse resource-constrained edge nodes in the real world. This limitation further leads to the inevitable model heterogeneity problem. In addition, performance bottlenecks and inefficient aggregation caused by inevitable data heterogeneity also limit the deployment of FedFM. In this paper, we propose a fine-grained parameter-efficient federated co-tuning framework based on knowledge decoupling, named FedKD, to simultaneously mitigate the aforementioned issues. It integrates a compact personalized tensor low-rank adapter (PTLoRA) and an efficient two-stage distillation scheme (KDMD). Specifically, PTLoRA explicitly decouples the low-rank weight update tensor of FM and adopts the layer-sharing scheme to enable efficient fine-tuning for enhanced edge models. It enables efficient fine-tuning by tackling inconsistent task-relevant knowledge across layers caused by data heterogeneity. Furthermore, KDMD implicitly decouples the knowledge learned from private datasets and transfers the decoupled general knowledge to the cloud FM. It alleviates the model divergence during aggregation, thereby improving the generalization of the cloud FM. Extensive simulations in various heterogeneous scenarios demonstrate that FedKD improves the generalization of the cloud model and the personalization of edge models. These results highlight the effectiveness of FedKD for supporting various cloud-edge collaborations. Code is available online athttps://github.com/Aprilmin/FedKD.

title: Examinattion of Benign/Malignant Breast Cancer Histopathology Slides Using Fused Deep Features
abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is the prime health concern in women community and major reason for the death worldwide. Clinical level examination of the BC is performed using biomedical image based examination in which the histopathology slide plays a major role in confirming the cancer and its stage. Hence, several methods are proposed to analyze these images to achieve accurate BC detection. This study aims to plan a deep-learning (DL) procedure for detecting the benign/malignant class BC using the conventional and fused-features along with the softmax. The different phases available in the considered image examination procedure involves in; (i) data collection and resizing, (ii) image examination with deep-features obtained with the considered DL-scheme, (iii) binary classification implementation with softmax, (iv) identification of best two DL-model features for generating the fused-features (FF), and (v) classification and confirmation with 3-fold cross validation (TFC). This work achieved a detection accuracy of$>90 \%$with individual features and$>99 \%$with FF when softmax based classification is executed.

title: MC-BCNet: MobileNet Family-Based Feature-Fusion CNN with Grad-CAM and Monte Carlo Dropout for Efficient Breast Cancer Screening
abstract: The accurate and timely diagnosis of breast cancer is critical for improving patient survival; however, manual interpretation of medical images is time-consuming and prone to inter-observer variability. Although deep learning–based approaches have demonstrated strong diagnostic performance, many state-of-the-art models are computationally intensive and lack transparency, limiting their adoption in real-world clinical environments. This study proposes MC-BCNet, a resourceefficient and trustworthy diagnostic framework that evaluates lightweight Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) from the MobileNet family for automated breast cancer screening. A comparative analysis of MobileNet, MobileNetV2, MobileNetV3-Large, and MobileNetV3-Small is conducted using transfer learning backbones integrated into a highly feature-extractive CNN architecture. Experiments are performed on two medical imaging modalities: the BreakHis histopathology dataset (1,600 images with offline data augmentation and oversampling) and a breast ultrasound dataset (3,000 images). Stratified train–validation-test splitting is employed to ensure unbiased evaluation, and performance is assessed using accuracy, sensitivity, and ROC–AUC metrics. To enhance clinical trustworthiness, the framework incorporates Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (GradCAM) for visual explainability and Monte Carlo Dropout for predictive uncertainty quantification. Experimental results show that the baseline MobileNet achieves superior sensitivity on complex histopathology images with 91% accuracy, while all MobileNet variants attain 99% accuracy on ultrasound scans. High-confidence predictions are confirmed through uncertainty histograms, and Grad-CAM visualizations successfully highlight clinically relevant tumor regions. Overall, the proposed framework effectively balances computational efficiency, diagnostic accuracy, and interpretability, offering a reliable solution for automated breast cancer screening in resource-constrained healthcare settings.

title: GlobalSplat: Efficient Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting via Global Scene Tokens
abstract: The efficient spatial allocation of primitives serves as the foundation of 3D Gaussian Splatting, as it directly dictates the synergy between representation compactness, reconstruction speed, and rendering fidelity. Previous solutions, whether based on iterative optimization or feed-forward inference, suffer from significant trade-offs between these goals, mainly due to the reliance on local, heuristic-driven allocation strategies that lack global scene awareness. Specifically, current feed-forward methods are largely pixel-aligned or voxel-aligned. By unprojecting pixels into dense, view-aligned primitives, they bake redundancy into the 3D asset. As more input views are added, the representation size increases and global consistency becomes fragile. To this end, we introduce GlobalSplat, a framework built on the principle of align first, decode later. Our approach learns a compact, global, latent scene representation that encodes multi-view input and resolves cross-view correspondences before decoding any explicit 3D geometry. Crucially, this formulation enables compact, globally consistent reconstructions without relying on pretrained pixel-prediction backbones or reusing latent features from dense baselines. Utilizing a coarse-to-fine training curriculum that gradually increases decoded capacity, GlobalSplat natively prevents representation bloat. On RealEstate10K and ACID, our model achieves competitive novel-view synthesis performance while utilizing as few as 16K Gaussians, significantly less than required by dense pipelines, obtaining a light 4MB footprint. Further, GlobalSplat enables significantly faster inference than the baselines, operating under 78 milliseconds in a single forward pass. Project page is available at https://r-itk.github.io/globalsplat/

title: Collaborative Multi-Agent Method for Zero-Shot LLM-Generated Text Detection
abstract: With the rapid proliferation of large language models (LLMs), distinguishing machine-generated text from human-authored content has become increasingly critical for ensuring content authenticity, academic integrity, and trust in information systems. However, detecting text generated by LLMs remains a challenging problem, particularly in zero-shot settings where labeled data and domain-specific tuning are unavailable. To address this challenge, in this paper, we propose a novel Collaborative Multi-Agent Zero-Shot Detection framework (CMA-ZSD). In contrast to existing methods based on watermarking, statistical heuristics, or neural classifiers, our CMA-ZSD employs three functionally heterogeneous agents that perform differentiated perturbations of the input text. By jointly modeling semantic consistency, grammatical normalization, and feature-level reconstruction, our method captures intrinsic asymmetries between human-authored and LLM-generated text. A semantic similarity evaluation mechanism, combined with majority voting, enables robust and interpretable detection decisions that balance individual agent autonomy with collective consensus. Extensive experiments across 11 domains demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, with its zero-shot detection achieving accuracy comparable to domain-finetuned models in specific domains such as Finance and Reddit-dli5.

title: SIMULATION AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: THE CONVERGENCE OF AI AND HIGH-PERFORMANCE COMPUTING
abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing (HPC) is transforming scientific research, industrial innovation, and digital infrastructures worldwide. AI systems increasingly require enormous computational resources, large-scale data processing capabilities, and highly specialized hardware architectures. At the same time, traditional scientific simulation continues to depend on HPC infrastructures for modeling complex physical phenomena. This article examines the emerging convergence between simulation and AI, emphasizing the technological, methodological, and organizational implications of this transformation. We will look into the current trends that are drive by the commercial market rather than by science. Next, we will explore the requirements that AI has compared to simulation. For this we will explore a model for simulation and see how it can be adapted to AI. Given the current changes both in industry and science we propose a concept for a convergence of AI and HPC which we call “Digital Convergence”. Keywords: artificial intelligence, types of modeling, digital convergence.

evidence.title: SIMULATION AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: THE CONVERGENCE OF AI AND HIGH-PERFORMANCE COMPUTING
evidence.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing (HPC) is transforming scientific research, industrial innovation, and digital infrastructures worldwide. AI systems increasingly require enormous computational resources, large-scale data processing capabilities, and highly specialized hardware architectures. At the same time, traditional scientific simulation continues to depend on HPC infrastructures for modeling complex physical phenomena. This article examines the emerging convergence between simulation and AI, emphasizing the technological, methodological, and organizational implications of this transformation. We will look into the current trends that are drive by the commercial market rather than by science. Next, we will explore the requirements that AI has compared to simulation. For this we will explore a model for simulation and see how it can be adapted to AI. Given the current changes both in industry and science we propose a concept for a convergence of AI and HPC which we call “Digital Convergence”. Keywords: artificial intelligence, types of modeling, digital convergence.

title: "Code and Data for the manuscript entitled Benchmarking Causal Discovery: Ground Truth and Interventional Validation"
abstract: "Most causal discovery benchmarks rely solely on consensus ground truth, leaving their ability to recover true causal mechanisms unclear. Using the Sachs protein signaling network, we benchmarked six causal discovery methods against both a gold-standard network and, critically, direct interventional data. Our results reveal a striking gap: only 16% of predicted edges survive interventional validation. DirectLiNGAM and ICALiNGAM offer the best balance of precision and recall, while deep learning methods produce substantially more false positives. We identify PKC\u2192Jnk as the most reliably inferred causal relationship. This study establishes a rigorous, intervention-based benchmark, provides practical guidance for method selection in small-sample biology, and demonstrates that agreement with domain knowledge alone is an insufficient measure of causal validity."

title: Cognitive Fallibility in LLMs: Modeling Human Forgetting and Reconstruction Bias to Enhance Trust
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit unnaturally perfect memory and unswerving confidence, which causes confidence and hallucinations, and loss of faith in human AI interactions. Following the line of thought of cognitive psychology, we propose the light weight and inferencetime Cognitive Architectures of LLMs (CALM): temporal forgetting basedon Ebbinghaus Decay and contextual reconstruction bias based on sentiment modulated retrieval. CALM is a nonretraining language model using a dynamic memory buffer and adding it to any LLM (e.g., Llama-3) and controlling the retrieval process depending on time and emotion. Evaluated on the Deese-Roediger-McDermott (DRM) paradigm and TruthfulQA, CALM produces near human rates of false recall (38.2 % vs.$35-40 \%$), and decreases the rate of overconfidence scores by 37 % and increases the rate of human trust ratings by 47 %, despite lower rates of factual accuracy. Human assessments show that the users find CALM to be more relatable, humble and trustworthy than infallible baselines. These findings upset the paradigm that has embraced accuracy and equated reliability with correctness, and the findings show that fallibility is better controlled to increase trust. CALM sets a new design principle of the trustworthy AI: not to memorize everything, but to memorize like us.

title: Homograph Disambiguation in Bangla Grapheme-to-Phoneme Conversion Using Large Language Models
abstract: Grapheme-to-phoneme (G2P) conversion for Bangla presents unique challenges due to its complex morphological structure and low-resource nature. Homograph disambiguation is one of the major challenges in G2P conversion, as creating a balanced and diverse homograph dataset is costly and time-consuming. In this paper, we propose a pipeline for preparing a homograph-enriched dataset for the Bangla language. Our dataset contains 206 homographs across 31,506 sentences. This gives us roughly 74 samples for each distinct pronunciation. We finetuned Large Language Models (LLMs), specifically Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer (T5), utilizing our dataset. One of our fine-tuned models achieved a Word Error Rate (WER) of 3.4 %, a Phoneme Error Rate (PER) of 0.78 %, and a homograph accuracy of 92.28 % on 5,091 test samples. This result indicates robust performance in homograph disambiguation as well as phoneme prediction for Bangla texts. Additionally, we evaluated inference latency to compare the models.

title: Hybrid physical/logical zero-noise extrapolation with limited logical executions
abstract: Partially error-corrected logical executions are expected to become available before fully fault-tolerant quantum computation, but such executions usually take much longer runtime than physical, unencoded ones. We formulate zero-noise extrapolation in this regime as a statistical resource-allocation problem in which the physical/logical execution mode is itself an extrapolation design variable. In the proposed mixed strategy, one or a few logical circuits provide low-noise anchor points, while cheaper folded physical circuits provide a larger extrapolation lever arm. Within an effective error suppression model $p_L=γp$, we derive Richardson variance prefactors for all-logical and mixed data sets, include folded-circuit runtime accounting, obtain the optimal shot allocation for a prescribed target variance, and state the bias--variance criterion determining when the mixed estimator improves finite-runtime accuracy. We illustrate the mixed-data strategy via simulating dynamics of transverse-field Ising model. For error suppression factor $γ\lesssim 0.1$ the mixed strategy can significantly(orders-of-magnitude) reduce the runtime needed to reach a fixed estimator variance, as well as provide better mean-square-error estimators in reasonable parameter regions.

title: AI and Statistics: An Examination of the Capabilities of AI Models to Perform Data Science
abstract: Artificial intelligence has become one of the fastest growing modern technologies, with publicly available AI chatbots becoming particularly popular since the 2022 launch of OpenAI’s ChatGPT. Due to their seemingly endless applications and unrivalled ease of use, these AI models present a new and often highly efficient method of approaching problems, completing tasks, but with some many marketed models available, it is challenging to know which is the best one to use. This experiment tests 4 of the most popular AI models at performing data science tasks with given datasets, a common application of AI. These models are OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Anthropic’s Claude, Microsoft’s Copilot, and Perplexity AI Inc.’s Perplexity. The results reveal which model actually performs with the least errors, where the overall benchmark lies, and how capable AI is at performing statistical data analysis with minimal human input.

title: ROBÓTICA EDUCACIONAL NO NOVO ENSINO MÉDIO: UM ESTUDO QUALITATIVO SOBRE O IMPACTO DO CLUBE EM COMPETÊNCIAS STEAM E SOCIOEMOCIONAIS.
authors: Francisco das Chagas de Brito Paiva
abstract: Este estudo investigou a robótica educacional como ferramenta pedagógica para o desenvolvimento de competências do século XXI em alunos do Ensino Médio. A pesquisa, de abordagem qualitativa, foi realizada numa escola pública através de um clube de robótica envolvendo oito alunos. Utilizando a metodologia STEAM e kits LEGO® Education, analisou-se o impacto da prática no pensamento crítico, resolução de problemas, criatividade e colaboração. Os resultados demonstram que a robótica, ao integrar conceitos disciplinares de forma prática e lúdica, promoveu avanços significativos no desempenho técnico e nas competências socioemocionais. A atividade fomentou o engajamento, a autonomia e a proatividade, posicionando os estudantes como protagonistas do próprio aprendizado. Conclui-se que a robótica educacional é uma estratégia eficaz para a formação integral, validando a sua aplicação como uma poderosa ferramenta para a educação contemporânea e para o enfrentamento de desafios complexos.

title: FedTanush: Second-Order Federated Learning Without Communication Cost Explosion
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) on edge devices is fundamentally constrained by the trilemma of statistical heterogeneity (client drift), limited communication bandwidth, and hardware thermal instability. In this study, we propose a novel federated optimization algorithm designed to achieve high-performance global model convergence while remaining hardware-aware. At its core, the proposed work leverages Diagonal Fisher Information as a Gauss-Newton approximation of the Hessian matrix, providing second-order curvature awareness without the O(d^2) computational overhead. This curvature information is integrated into a Spectral Momentum (Preconditioned Update) mechanism, which adaptively scales local updates by the inverse of the loss landscape spectrum. This effectively mitigates client drift by decelerating updates in high-curvature regions and accelerating them in the flat minima. To address the communication bottleneck, the proposed framework employs Top-K Density-Adaptive Sparsification, transmitting only the most significant 10% of gradient updates. To ensure that no critical information is lost, we implement a Residual Error Feedback buffer that accumulates discarded fine-detail updates for future rounds, maintaining mathematical convergence guarantees. Distinct from traditional FL frameworks, this study introduces Thermal Duty-Cycling; by utilizing temporal yielding and intra-batch micro-sleeps, the algorithm aligns with Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS) principles to prevent SoC throttling during intensive second-order calculations. Implemented via the Flower (flwr) framework with a client-side AdamW optimizer for decoupled weight decay, the proposed algorithm achieves a peak accuracy of 98.76% for Non IID MNIST data distribution. Experimental results demonstrate an 11x reduction in model drift and up to 58.48% bandwidth saving when comparative accuracy is achieved, all while maintaining a stable thermal state on resource-constrained edge devices.

title: Ontosphere
abstract: Ontosphere is a browser-based RDF/ontology knowledge graph editor. It loads RDF from local files, remote URLs, or SPARQL/Fuseki endpoints; lets users author nodes and edges directly on the canvas; runs OWL-RL reasoning with visual differentiation of inferred triples; and applies multi-algorithm layout (Dagre, ELK) and automatic clustering for large graphs. Additional features include namespace management with live URI renaming, a drag-and-drop workflow template catalog, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for AI-agent integration. All computation runs entirely client-side in the browser against an in-memory RDF store backed by Web Workers — no backend required.

title: A Zero Trust Driven Federative Learning Algorithm for Privacy Enhancement
abstract: The proliferation of Enterprise Networks, characterized by heterogeneous devices, distributed data sources, and increasingly sophisticated cyber threats, has exposed the limitations of traditional perimeter-based security models. Guided by the principles of Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA), this paper presents a Zero-Trust (ZT)-Driven Federated Learning Algorithm for Privacy Enhancement (ZT-FL-PE), designed to safeguard model and data confidentiality in decentralized learning environments. By integrating ZTA’s “never trust, always verify” posture with Federated Learning’s (FL) decentralized training paradigm, the proposed framework eliminates the need for centralized data aggregation and significantly reduces the attack surface. The algorithm specifically targets two prominent threats to model privacy: property inference attacks (PIAs) and membership inference attacks (MIAs). We introduce adaptive verification mechanisms and privacy-preserving update transformations that enforce continuous authentication, constrain adversarial behavior, and strengthen resilience against inference-based exploitation. Experimental results demonstrate that ZT-FL-PE substantially enhances privacy protection while maintaining high model accuracy and imposing only low-to-moderate computational overhead, making it a practical and robust solution for modern ZT Enterprise environments.

title: Generative AI for Cross-Technology Communication in Consumer Electronics
abstract: Cross-Technology Communication (CTC) enables interoperability between wireless technologies such asWiFi, BLE, LoRa, and ZigBee in Consumer Electronics (CE). However, existing methods face limitations in scalability and adaptability, particularly under real-world impairments like Carrier Frequency Offset (CFO) and Adjacent-Channel Interference (ACI). To address these challenges, we propose GAI-CTC, a Generative AI-driven framework for CTC that optimizes waveform synthesis, spectrum adaptation, and semantic alignment in a unified, end-to-end neural architecture. GAI-CTC utilizes a multi-domain neural network that generates waveforms for multiple protocols while complying with spectral-mask, power, and latency constraints. The framework leverages a cyclic generative learning mechanism and semantic consistency loss to ensure efficient transmitter-receiver mapping. The model is trained through joint optimization of key loss components, includingLCTC,Lmask, andLsem. Simulation results show that GAI-CTC achieves up to 3 × higher goodput and 20-40% lower energy-per-bit compared to Baseline CTC. Additionally, GAI-CTC improves spectral mask compliance by 30-50 percentage points and enhances CFO tolerance by 20 ppm, demonstrating its potential to enable efficient and adaptive communication in multi-protocol wireless systems.

title: Explainable Sentence Classification in Biomedical Abstracts: Benchmarking NLP Models with DistilBERT and Saliency Maps
abstract: Medical abstracts often lack clear sentence-level structure, making it difficult for researchers and professionals to quickly extract essential information. In databases like PubMed, most abstracts are not annotated with sentence-level functional labels such as Background, Methods or Results. This study aims to automatically classify individual sentences in biomedical abstracts using deep learning techniques. We evaluated four models: a baseline Naive Bayes classifier using TF-IDF vectors, a 1D Convolutional Neural Network (Conv1D) with trainable embeddings, the Universal Sentence Encoder (USE) for semantic representations and DistilBERT, a lightweight Transformer-based model. Experiments were conducted using the PubMed 20k RCT dataset, a subset of approximately 20,000 annotated abstracts from randomized controlled trials. Results show that DistilBERT outperforms other models with an F1-score of 85.68%. USE underperforms due to domain mismatch. To enhance model interpretability, Saliency Maps were used, revealing the influence of biomedical terminology on predictions. This research demonstrates the potential of deep learning for structuring biomedical literature to support faster information retrieval.

title: A Multiclass Financial Transaction Fraud Prediction Scheme Using Machine Learning, Ensemble Feature Selection, and XAI Technique
abstract: Predicting financial transaction fraud is crucial since it costs both consumers and businesses a lot of money. Prior research on predicting financial transaction fraud has only used binary classification. Lower accuracy, improper data preparation, annotation, feature engineering, hyper parameter selection, and model interpretation outcomes are some of the problems with the earlier work. By taking into account ATO, phishing, bank account, refund, and card skimming fraud, this study offers a multiclass financial transaction fraud prediction technique based on machine learning to address the previous issues. By comparing its performance with five machine learning classifiers, the LGBM model with 99.8% accuracy and 96.5% F1 score is chosen as an appropriate prediction model. Advanced data annotation, preprocessing, SHAP-based model interpretation, SMOTE NC based class imbalance reduction, ensemble feature selection, and optunabased hyper parameter tuning approaches were all employed in proposed LGBM prediction model. The accuracy and F1 score of the proposed LGBM model are 2.8% higher than those of previous studies.

title: SegWithU: Uncertainty as Perturbation Energy for Single-Forward-Pass Risk-Aware Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: Reliable uncertainty estimation is critical for medical image segmentation, where automated contours feed downstream quantification and clinical decision support. Many strong uncertainty methods require repeated inference, while efficient single-forward-pass alternatives often provide weaker failure ranking or rely on restrictive feature-space assumptions. We present SegWithU, a post-hoc framework that augments a frozen pretrained segmentation backbone with a lightweight uncertainty head. SegWithU taps intermediate backbone features and models uncertainty as perturbation energy in a compact probe space using rank-1 posterior probes. It produces two voxel-wise uncertainty maps: a calibration-oriented map for probability tempering and a ranking-oriented map for error detection and selective prediction. Across ACDC, BraTS2024, and LiTS, SegWithU is the strongest and most consistent single-forward-pass baseline, achieving AUROC/AURC of 0.9838/2.4885, 0.9946/0.2660, and 0.9925/0.8193, respectively, while preserving segmentation quality. These results suggest that perturbation-based uncertainty modeling is an effective and practical route to reliability-aware medical segmentation. Source code is available at https://github.com/ProjectNeura/SegWithU.

title: From a What to a Who: The Five Core Components of Behavioral Architecture
abstract: What separates a thing from a self? An object responds to forces. A self responds to situations — evaluating them, choosing among options, and acting in its own interest. Ethology explains behavior through Tinbergen's four questions — causation, development, function, and phylogeny — but each takes a behavior as its object. None asks the prior question: what is the organism producing that behavior currently made of? This paper poses that as a fifth question and answers it with the five core components that turn a what into a who: Body, Personality (Cached Pattern Library), Beliefs, Emotions (Rapid Significance Classification), and Instincts. Each is distinct in origin, mechanism, developmental timing, and malleability; none constitutes any other. Together they define who the organism is — the behavioral architecture from which all behavior emerges, and whose current configuration can be read in a specific individual to predict and change its behavior. Motivation is not a sixth component but the real-time manifestation of self-interest arising as the five components interact with the current situation; a six-step deliberative process translates who the organism is into what it does. The framework applies to any organism with a nervous system capable of operant behavior, with direct implications for artificial intelligence systems whose behavioral architecture is currently missing critical components.

title: AtomRAG: atomic query decomposition for multi-hop retrieval-augmented generation
abstract: Introduction: Standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) often fails on multi-hop queries that require the synthesis of information from multiple sources. To address this limitation, we propose AtomRAG, a chain-of-prompts algorithm that decomposes a complex query into a series of atomic requirements for information retrieval. Materials and methods: This method utilizes a sequence of planning, parsing, and reasoning prompts to guide a large language model (LLM) in creating an explicit retrieval and synthesis plan before generating a final answer. We evaluated AtomRAG on FRAMES and BRIGHT benchmarks, comparing its performance against standard RAG and non-RAG baselines using an instruction-tuned model (Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) and a reasoning model (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B). Results: Our results reveal a significant performance divergence. For the instruction-tuned model, AtomRAG improved accuracy by a relative 14.8% on the complex reasoning tasks in FRAMES. Conversely, the reasoning model proved incompatible with the instructive planning prompts, resulting in a performance degradation. On the less complex BRIGHT benchmark simpler methods performed better. Conclusions: We conclude that the effectiveness of AtomRAG is highly dependent on both query complexity and model architecture.

title: Feature Integration from Pre-Trained CNN Extractors and ML Classifiers for Robust Lung Cancer Classification
abstract: Lung cancer is a leading cause of cancer-related fatalities worldwide. Early and precise identification of lung cancer by histopathological imaging is critical for efficient therapy and improved patient outcomes. This research describes a hybrid deep learning architecture that uses multiple pretrained convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for feature extraction and an XGBoost classifier to improve lung cancer classification performance. EfficientNetB0, DenseNet201, and VGG19 are used to extract distinct features from lung histopathology images. These features are then concatenated and fed into an XGBoost model, resulting in accurate multiclass classification. In addition, a weighted Grad-CAM visualization method is used to emphasize the most informative regions of the tissue images, making the model's predictions easier to comprehend. Experimental results show that the proposed hybrid CNN-XGBoost strategy outperforms individual CNN models for detecting various types of lung cancer. This technology appears to have the potential to increase the accuracy and efficiency with which pathologists detect lung cancer.

title: Breast Cancer Histology Image Classification using Transfer Learning and Grad-CAM-Based Explainability
abstract: Breast cancer has been regarded as one of the main causes of cancer-related deaths among women, where early and proper diagnosis becomes important in enhancing survival rates. This paper introduces a multiclass breast cancer histopathology classification system based on an automated deep learning system on the BACH data. The suggested pipeline includes image preprocessing, extracting$256 \times 256$patch-based features based on overlapping patches in order to achieve fine-grained tissue morphology, data augmentation to enhance generalization, and transfer learning using three pre-trained convolutional neural networks, i.e. AlexNet, Xception, and DenseNet201. Experimental findings prove that DenseNet201 can perform better with 96% validation accuracy, having balanced precision, recall, and F1-score of 98%, which is higher than the existing techniques. Interpretability of models is additionally examined through Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM), and it is established that predictions centre on clinically significant objects like cellular nuclei density and tissue structures as opposed to artifacts. In contrast to the existing work, the strength of the proposed framework can be assessed, which implies its potential to serve as a credible and interpretable computer-aided diagnostic method of clinical histopathological analysis.

title: Property testing in Gaussian graphical models: trees and small separation numbers
abstract: Abstract We study property testing for graphical models in a setting where an algorithm may adaptively query individual entries of the covariance matrix $\Sigma $, and cost is measured by the number of queried entries. Under natural (strong) faithfulness assumptions, we design divide-and-conquer tests guided by balanced separators that operate on small submatrices and avoid global matrix inversion. Our first result is a tester for whether the underlying graph is a tree; with high probability it decides correctly using a subquadratic number of correlation queries, and for bounded maximum degree $\Delta $ the complexity is near-linear up to logarithmic factors. Our second result concerns graphs with a small separation number (hence small treewidth). We present two complementary procedures: a conditional descent test that never breaks when $\text{sn}(G)\le k$ and, upon termination, returns an $O(k\log (n/k))$ certificate; and a marginal descent test that, under a ‘good run’ condition, either certifies $\text{sn}(G)\le 2k$ or proves $\text{sn}(G)>k$. The approach extends beyond the Gaussian case whenever reliable conditional-independence queries are available (e.g., non-paranormal models), yielding tests that access only a vanishing fraction of the entries of $\Sigma $.

title: Temporal Contrastive Decoding: A Training-Free Method for Large Audio-Language Models
abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) generalize across speech, sound, and music, but unified decoders can exhibit a \emph{temporal smoothing bias}: transient acoustic cues may be underutilized in favor of temporally smooth context that is better supported by language priors, leading to less specific audio-grounded outputs. We propose \emph{Temporal Contrastive Decoding} (TCD), a training-free decoding method for unified LALMs that mitigates this effect at inference time. TCD constructs a temporally blurred slow-path view by smoothing the input waveform and re-encoding it, then contrasts next-token logits from the original and slow-path views. The contrastive signal is applied as a token-level logit update restricted to a small candidate set. A self-normalized stability score sets the blur window and update scale, and a step-wise gate based on uncertainty and audio reliance activates the update only when needed. Experiments on MMAU and AIR-Bench show consistent improvements on strong unified LALMs. We further conduct ablations and an architectural applicability study to analyze the contributions of key components and how TCD behaves across large audio-language model designs.

title: Optimal last-iterate convergence in matrix games with bandit feedback using the log-barrier
abstract: We study the problem of learning minimax policies in zero-sum matrix games. Fiegel et al. (2025) recently showed that achieving last-iterate convergence in this setting is harder when the players are uncoupled, by proving a lower bound on the exploitability gap of Omega(t^{-1/4}). Some online mirror descent algorithms were proposed in the literature for this problem, but none have truly attained this rate yet. We show that the use of a log-barrier regularization, along with a dual-focused analysis, allows this O-tilde(t^{-1/4}) convergence with high-probability. We additionally extend our idea to the setting of extensive-form games, proving a bound with the same rate.

evidence.title: Optimal last-iterate convergence in matrix games with bandit feedback using the log-barrier
evidence.abstract: We study the problem of learning minimax policies in zero-sum matrix games. Fiegel et al. (2025) recently showed that achieving last-iterate convergence in this setting is harder when the players are uncoupled, by proving a lower bound on the exploitability gap of Omega(t^{-1/4}). Some online mirror descent algorithms were proposed in the literature for this problem, but none have truly attained this rate yet. We show that the use of a log-barrier regularization, along with a dual-focused analysis, allows this O-tilde(t^{-1/4}) convergence with high-probability. We additionally extend our idea to the setting of extensive-form games, proving a bound with the same rate.

title: Constraints on phantom codes from automorphism group bounds
abstract: Executing a logical quantum circuit fault-tolerantly incurs a large spacetime overhead. Recent work has proposed and investigated phantom codes, defined by the property that every in-block logical $\mathrm{CNOT}$ circuit can be implemented with a physical permutation, a property that has the potential to greatly reduce the depth of compiled circuits. Here we show that phantomness comes at the cost of low encoding rate. Specifically, we prove that any binary phantom code encoding $k$ logical qubits into $n$ physical qubits with distance $d\geq 2$ obeys the bound $k\leq \log_2(n+1)$ for all $k\neq 4$. For $k=4$ we explicitly construct a nonstabiliser $(\!(8, 2^4, 2)\!)$ phantom code that violates the bound and has a transversal non-Clifford gate. We further show that, within the class of nontrivial CSS phantom codes with $k\neq 4$, there is a unique family of codes saturating this bound. In addition, we prove that this logarithmic ceiling cannot be circumvented by permitting additional local unitary gates, or by making use of subsystem codes: any subspace or subsystem code admitting a $\mathrm{SWAP}$-transversal implementation of every logical $\mathrm{CNOT}$ circuit is constrained to satisfy the same bound. These bounds follow from a general theorem relating the length of a quantum code to the structure of its automorphism group, a result which may find applications beyond phantom codes.

title: Agentic Explainability at Scale: Between Corporate Fears and XAI Needs
abstract: As companies enter the race for agentic AI adoption, fears surface around agentic autonomy and its subsequent risks. These fears compound as companies scale their agentic AI adoption with low-code applications, without a comparable scaling in their governance processes and expertise resulting in a phenomenon known as "Agent Sprawl". While shadow AI tools can help with agentic discovery and identification, few observability tools offer insights into the agents' configuration and settings or the decision-making process during agent-to-agent communication and orchestration. This paper explores AI governance professionals' concerns in enterprise settings, while offering design-time and runtime explainability techniques as suggested by AI governance experts for addressing those fears. Finally, we provide a preliminary prototype of an Agentic AI Card that can help companies feel at ease deploying agents at scale.

title: IE as Cache: Information Extraction Enhanced Agentic Reasoning
abstract: Information Extraction aims to distill structured, decision-relevant information from unstructured text, serving as a foundation for downstream understanding and reasoning. However, it is traditionally treated merely as a terminal objective: once extracted, the resulting structure is often consumed in isolation rather than maintained and reused during multi-step inference. Moving beyond this, we propose \textit{IE-as-Cache}, a framework that repurposes IE as a cognitive cache to enhance agentic reasoning. Drawing inspiration from hierarchical computer memory, our approach combines query-driven extraction with cache-aware reasoning to dynamically maintain compact intermediate information and filter noise. Experiments on challenging benchmarks across diverse LLMs demonstrate significant improvements in reasoning accuracy, indicating that IE can be effectively repurposed as a reusable cognitive resource and offering a promising direction for future research on downstream uses of IE.

title: Cognitive Memory for LLM Agents: An Architecture Validated by Three Independent Discoveries
abstract: Large Language Models have no personalized memory. We present the Semantic Tension Graph (STG), a cognitive memory architecture for LLM agents that implements nine biologically-grounded mechanisms: activation propagation, Hebbian learning, synaptic pruning, salience decay, tension tracking, self-modeling, multi-phase inhibition, co-activation edge creation, and temporal episode structure. Post-hoc analysis reveals that STGindependently converged on the same architectural principles as Kanerva's Sparse Distributed Memory (1988) and Eliasmith's Semantic Pointer Architecture (2013). We identify four design constraints that any associative memory must satisfy, show three-way convergence across 38 yearsand three disciplines, and extend the analysis to 33 recent publications. Validated through longitudinal deployment (8,199 nodes, 20+ sessions),STG demonstrates cognitive continuity — resuming complex multi-domain research from a single natural language cue.

title: Phase-Synchronization-Based Federated Learning for Edge Computing Over Decentralized Networks
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training over decentralized edge devices while preserving data privacy; however, its performance is often degraded by client drift caused by non-IID data distributions and partial client participation. Motivated by the need for a principled mechanism to suppress directional inconsistency among distributed updates, we propose FedKuramoto, a novel FL algorithm inspired by the phase-synchronization dynamics of the Kuramoto oscillator model. In FedKuramoto, each client update is interpreted as an oscillator whose phase is defined by its angular deviation from the global update direction. The proposed method enforces phase coherence via a phase-constrained projection and introduces a coherence-aware momentum that acts as a restoring force, without incurring additional communication overhead. Extensive experiments on various benchmarks under varying heterogeneity and participation ratios demonstrate that FedKuramoto consistently accelerates convergence and improves accuracy over conventional FL algorithms. These results indicate that importing synchronization mechanisms from nonlinear dynamical systems offers an effective and robust design paradigm for decentralized learning.

title: Explainable and Multi-Modal Cross-Context Object Localization Using YOLOv5, K-Means Color Analysis, and Regional Heatmaps
abstract: An empirical investigation focuses on enhancing the explainability of deep neural networks (DNNs)-based object detection systems, with a particular emphasis on models like YOLOv5, which are frequently employed for precise visual recognition. However, deep models' explainability issue becomes a significant barrier, particularly in safety-critical applications where understanding model decisions is essential. Although those models optimize performance, models like YOLOv5 frequently serve as black boxes by obscuring how object information is derived from visual data. This study addresses this gap by suggesting an eXplainable AI (XAI)-driven multimodal interpretability framework for post-hoc analysis of object detection results. The proposed pipeline leverages pretrained YOLOv5 model for object localization across a curated$\mathbf{1 0 0 0}$cross-context COCO image set and the model acts as a basis for subsequent explainability analysis rather than performance measurement. For addressing the challenge of model transparency, K-Means-based color profiling, and model-agnostic regional heatmap visualization are integrated with YOLOv5x to enhance semantic and spatial interpretability. K-Means clustering provides quantitative acumen of localized objects by defining dominant (RGB) color clusters and variance. The regional heatmap emphasizes spatial detection confidence, aiding users realize how and where the model focuses during prediction. By attaining heatmap alignment score of 84.25 %, saliency consistency of 99.21 %, regional concentration of 61.45 %, and combined score of 77.06 %, the experiment reveals that the proposed framework demonstrates better interpretability than both Grad-CAM and RISE. The experimental result suggests that by prioritizing interpretability, stability, and behavioral insight over accuracy measurement, the proposed framework offers an annotation-free, scalable, and robust explainability maintaining transparency and providing direction for future realworld system improvement.

title: SNM-Transnet: A Novel SNMish Activation-Based Attention Enhanced Hybrid Architecture for Accurate Breast Cancer Image Classification
abstract: Breast cancer (BC) remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide, highlighting the urgent need for accurate and early diagnosis. Although deep learning models have shown promise in automating histopathological image classification, traditional CNNs often struggle to capture global contextual information and may suffer from issues such as vanishing gradients. This paper proposes SNM-TransNet, a novel hybrid architecture designed to address these limitations for precise BC classification. The model combines a CNN backbone for local feature extraction with a multi-head self-attention Transformer encoder to model long-range dependencies within tissue structures. A key innovation is the Dual Statistical Normalized Mish (SNMish) activation function, a normalized variant of the Mish activation function, which enhances gradient flow, stabilizes training, and improves feature representation compared to the standard ReLU. Evaluated on the BreakHis dataset across multiple magnifications (40X, 100X, 200X, 400X), SNM-TransNet consistently outperforms a ReLU-based variant, ReLU-TransNet, and several pre-trained state-of-the-art models. At 100 X magnification, it achieved a peak accuracy of 97.60 %, a precision of 99.33 %, and an ROC-AUC value of 99.24 %. To ensure clinical trust and interpretability, LIME was integrated, providing transparent visualizations by highlighting diagnostically relevant regions. These results demonstrate that SNM-TransNet offers a robust, accurate, and interpretable framework for BC diagnosis.

title: Cosm: orchestrated collective dynamics give rise to rapid computational search at the solution frontier
abstract: We introduce Collective Switched Motion (Cosm), a heuristic optimization framework based on orchestrated collective dynamics. Cosm organizes the objective into conflict-minimized subobjectives and activates them sequentially, temporally separating competing local influences. The interplay of switching and local interactions among variables, supplemented by structured correlated perturbations, gives rise to collective search behavior including coordinated cluster motion. Using this framework, we develop and test a solver for sparse Ising optimization. On G64, a large sparse instance with a highly heterogeneous degree distribution from the longstanding Gset Max-Cut benchmark suite, Cosm establishes a new best-known cut of 8753. On large random-graph instances G61 and G70, whose best-known cuts of 5799 and 9595 have been difficult for prior heuristics to attain, a vectorized CPU implementation of Cosm reliably reaches these cuts with times-to-target of 15 s and 2.4 s, respectively. Cosm also heuristically attains the certified optimum of G81, the largest Gset instance (a 20,000-variable two-dimensional spin glass), along with those of G72 and G77. Tests on planted-solution spin-glass benchmarks suggest more favorable empirical scaling than that previously reported for seven compared solvers. Cosm demonstrates that, from simple interacting elements and a new form of orchestration, effective search can emerge.

title: Heuristic Search for Minimum-Distance Upper-Bound Witnesses in Quantum APM-LDPC Codes
abstract: This paper investigates certified upper bounds on the minimum distance of an explicit family of Calderbank-Shor-Steane quantum LDPC codes constructed from affine permutation matrices. All codes considered here have active Tanner graphs of girth eight. Rather than attempting to prove a general lower bound for the full code distance, we focus on constructing low-weight non-stabilizer logical representatives, which yield valid upper bounds once they are verified to lie in the opposite parity-check kernel and outside the stabilizer row space. We develop a unified framework for such witnesses arising from latent row relations, restricted-lift subspaces including block-compressed, selected-fiber, and CRT-stripe constructions, cycle- 8 elementary trapping-set structures, and decoder-failure residuals. In every case, search is used only to generate candidates; the reported bounds begin only after explicit kernel and row-space exclusion tests have been passed. For the latent part, we also identify a block-compression criterion under which the certification becomes exact. Applying these methods to representative APM-LDPC codes sharpens previously reported upper bounds and provides concrete certified values across the explored parameter range.

title: TokenGS: Decoupling 3D Gaussian Prediction from Pixels with Learnable Tokens
abstract: In this work, we revisit several key design choices of modern Transformer-based approaches for feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) prediction. We argue that the common practice of regressing Gaussian means as depths along camera rays is suboptimal, and instead propose to directly regress 3D mean coordinates using only a self-supervised rendering loss. This formulation allows us to move from the standard encoder-only design to an encoder-decoder architecture with learnable Gaussian tokens, thereby unbinding the number of predicted primitives from input image resolution and number of views. Our resulting method, TokenGS, demonstrates improved robustness to pose noise and multiview inconsistencies, while naturally supporting efficient test-time optimization in token space without degrading learned priors. TokenGS achieves state-of-the-art feed-forward reconstruction performance on both static and dynamic scenes, producing more regularized geometry and more balanced 3DGS distribution, while seamlessly recovering emergent scene attributes such as static-dynamic decomposition and scene flow.

title: A NISQ-friendly Coined Quantum Walk Algorithm for Chaos-based Cryptographic Applications
abstract: We present a novel lackadaisical alternating quantum walk (LAQW) algorithm whose circuit depth scales as $\mathcal{O}(n^2+nt)$ for a $n\times n$ lattice over $t$ time steps. We show that this is a significant depth reduction compared to the existing controlled alternating quantum walk (CAQW) model, which has a circuit depth that scales as $\mathcal{O}(n^2t)$ (Li et al., 2017, arXiv:1707.07389). This makes the implementation of the LAQW viable for Noisy Intermediate-scale Quantum (NISQ) devices. We then showcase the applicability of the LAQW algorithm by proposing a chaos-based symmetric-key generation scheme. Our approach uses the LAQW as a quantum entropy source from which reproducible random bitstring sequences are generated using the underlying probability distribution and subsequent post-processing methods. We provide a comprehensive evaluation of the LAQW algorithm and demonstrate the reproducibility of 128-bit keys under simulated quantum noise provided by IBM's FakeTorino backend. A direct comparison with the CAQW model, which has been used in image encryption and hash function schemes (Li et al., 2017, arXiv:1707.07389; Abd EL-Latif et al., 2020, ScienceDirect; Abd El-Latif, Abd El-Atty, and Venegas-Andraca, 2020, ScienceDirect), highlights the potential and usefulness of the LAQW model in cryptographic applications.

title: Emotion Vectors and Constrained Transport: A Possible Bridge from Claude's Interpretability to Bounded Interiority
abstract: Bridge note — not peer reviewed Summary A short theoretical bridge note connecting Anthropic's recent interpretability findings on emotion vectors in Claude Sonnet 4.5 to the Computation as Constrained Transport and Curvature Adaptation Hypothesis frameworks. The note argues that Anthropic's emotion vectors — local, causally active, behavior-shaping control features — are functionally consistent with the view that emotions are compressed, load-bearing reorganizations of salience and action-readiness that emerge when neutral global reconstruction is too costly. The bridge is characterized as functional rather than ontological: transformer systems may approximate the control logic of emotional computation without possessing the metabolically bounded interior that, on the biological account, makes such reorganizations lived rather than merely executed. A key open question identified is whether post-training shifts in emotion vector recruitment represent genuine reflective governance or a more superficial suppression of high-intensity states. The Anthropic interpretability research referenced in this note can be found at: Emotion concepts and their function in a large language model. https://www.anthropic.com/research/emotion-concepts-function Related Works: Pender, M.
